In 2024, we were appointed Singapore’s first SkillsFuture Queen Bee for the Energy and Power sector, underscoring our commitment to advancing industry capabilities.
Through the S$25 million Sembcorp Energy for Good Fund, we drive decarbonisation in the charity sector. Since 2022, our solarisation projects have powered over 110 community sites, generating over 930,000kWh of clean energy and avoiding 654,000kgCO2e of greenhouse gas emissions, comparable to the annual electricity consumption of over 3501 four-room Housing & Development Board flats in Singapore.
Strengthening Energy Security We operate a diversified 28.5GW global energy portfolio, including gas-fired assets across Asia, the Middle East and the UK. These assets deliver reliable power, while enhancing grid resilience and supporting national energy security. Supporting Energy Accessibility Our balanced portfolio with a well-managed cost base and high reliability enables us to deliver essential energy to communities and industries.
Our gas portfolio provides stable, highly visible cash flow underpinned by offtake contracts, which supports our earnings base and funds our energy transition initiatives, such as renewables, low-carbon solutions and sustainable industrial parks.
We have built a strong track record across 11 countries, with growth through competitive greenfield tenders, as well as disciplined, returns-driven brownfield acquisitions.
To date, we have invested over S$5 billion in renewable energy projects globally, building a proven track record in delivering large-scale, complex transition investments.
We are also advancing low-carbon technologies, exploring green hydrogen and ammonia projects, including the 600MW hydrogen-ready combined cycle power plant on Jurong Island, set for operation by the fourth quarter of 2026.
In parallel, we enable cross-border decarbonisation through 2.2GW of low-carbon electricity imports from Vietnam and Malaysia.
Building Sustainable Communities and Industrial Ecosystems Enabling Energy Sustainability Empowering an Inclusive Transition >15,000 training hours across 108 partner companies Global energy portfolio at 28.5GW 8.1GW Gas and others* 20.4GW Renewable energy * Others include diesel and energy-from-waste 1 Conversion is based on the 2024 Grid Emission Factor published by the Energy Market Authority of Singapore and the 2024 average electricity consumption rates for households published by the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, Singapore We have expanded our renewables capacity by more than six-fold in just five years, growing from 3.2GW to 20.4GW through greenfield developments, strategic acquisitions and partnerships. Sembcorp Industries Annual Report 2025 4 5 Overview Operating and Financial Review Our Leadership Other Information Consolidated Financial Statements Environmental, Social and Governance Review Our Energy Transition Story Dear Shareholders, The operating environment in 2025 was marked by heightened geopolitical tensions, trade frictions and a slowing global economy. At the same time, the unprecedented and rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) continued to reshape industries and energy demand. Against this backdrop, we remained focused on execution, portfolio discipline and capital allocation. We have stayed the course on our purpose of driving energy transition responsibly, balancing the immediate need for energy security with our unwavering commitment to building a low-carbon future. Resilient Financial Performance Despite the uncertainties, the Group delivered a resilient performance. Our results reflected the strength of our diversified portfolio, disciplined cost management and execution of our strategic priorities. In financial year 2025 (FY2025), the Group achieved a turnover of S$5.8 billion and underlying net profit of S$1.0 billion. Our return on equity stood at 18.2%, reflecting our continued focus on capital efficiency. The Board is pleased to propose a final dividend of 16.0 cents per ordinary share, subject to shareholders’ approval. This brings total dividend for the year to 25.0 cents per ordinary share, an increase of 9% or 2.0 cents from FY2024. This reflects confidence in our long-term strategy and the visibility of our cash flows.
Driving Growth with Financial Discipline Our growth strategy is built on the strength of our business lines: ensuring energy security through our Gas and Related Services segment and driving the transition through our Renewables and Integrated Urban Solutions segments. Gas and Related Services: Providing Reliability through the Energy Transition As the energy transition accelerates, the need for reliable and dispatchable power has become more critical. Our 8GW global gas portfolio continues to underpin grid stability while enabling the integration of renewables and low-carbon energy sources into the power system. In Singapore, we increased our stake in Senoko Energy to 50%. With this stake, we will look to unlock operational synergies and enhance the efficiency of our Singapore power assets as well as support national energy security. At the same time, we are future-proofing our generation capabilities. We are on track to complete our new 600MW hydrogen-ready power plant in 2026, strengthening our ability to meet evolving energy needs. Together, our assets are well-positioned to support growing power requirements of the data centre and high-tech manufacturing industries in Singapore. In a world where AI-driven load growth is reshaping demand patterns, Sembcorp is already a trusted partner to these critical industries, supplying more than one-third of the data centre power needs in Singapore. In the UK, while operating conditions remain challenging due to subdued industrial demand, we continue to exercise cost discipline and are repositioning the business to broaden customer reach and capture emerging opportunities in data centres.
Renewables: Scaling with Execution and Reliability We continued to expand our renewables portfolio with discipline, focusing on market fundamentals and execution capabilities. Since 2021, we have invested over S$5 billion globally and grown our gross renewables capacity more than six-fold, from 3.2GW to 20.4GW, including an acquisition pending completion. Despite market challenges in the China renewables market due to elevated curtailment and tariff pressures, our expanding platforms in the region continued to provide resilience and deliver growth for the segment.
In India, we strengthened our position as a leading independent power producer. We secured a 150MW firm and dispatchable renewable energy project from SJVN, integrating solar and battery energy storage systems to support the growing demand for reliable, renewable power. Together with our other wins, our gross renewables capacity in India has now surpassed 7.6GW. In the Middle East, we achieved a significant milestone with the signing of a 20-year power purchase agreement for the 125MW Dhofar II wind power project. This is our first wind project in Oman, shortly after we commissioned the 588MWp Manah II Solar Independent Power Project. These assets support Oman’s Vision 2040 target of generating 30% of electricity from renewable sources. In Singapore, we continue to lead in maximising renewable potential in a land-scarce environment. We were awarded the 86MWp Pandan Reservoir floating solar project by PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency. We also signed a 25-year renewable energy purchase agreement with a subsidiary of Meta Platforms to build, own and operate a 150MWp floating solar farm at Kranji Reservoir. These long-term contracts further reinforce our position as the nation’s leading floating solar energy player. Integrated Urban Solutions: Building Sustainable Growth Platforms Our Urban business continued to grow. During the year, three new Vietnam Singapore Industrial Park (VSIP) projects were awarded investment registration certificates. We further expanded our footprint in January 2026, with a new investment approval for VSIP Hue in central Vietnam. With these investment approvals, our portfolio now comprises 22 industrial parks across 15 provinces and major cities in Vietnam. These new parks are designed to be smart, green and future-ready, and are well-positioned to serve as strategic hubs for clean-tech and export-focused industries. In Indonesia, we are also making strides with our Tembesi Innovation District, which has received strong pre-commitment interest. We also signed a Memorandum of Understanding with NeutraDC to jointly develop sustainable data centre infrastructure in Southeast Asia. Sharpening the Portfolio and Entering a New Growth Market Portfolio optimisation remains a core discipline. In March 2025, we completed the divestment of Sembcorp Environment, sharpening the Group’s focus on energy and urban solutions. Proceeds from this capital recycling exercise will be redeployed in line with our strategic priorities to support disciplined growth and value creation. Looking beyond our established markets, 2025 also marked a pivotal milestone in our geographical expansion. In December, we announced the proposed acquisition of Alinta Energy in Australia. The transaction provides immediate scale, entry into an AAA-rated country and access to a high-quality generation portfolio and development pipeline. The acquisition is immediately earnings accretive and broadens our growth capabilities in a well-established market. Powering an Inclusive Future We remain committed to contributing positively to the communities in which we operate. Through the Sembcorp Energy for Good framework, we support a range of community initiatives, including programmes aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 7.
During the year, we commissioned a 95kWp solar energy system at Boys’ Town in Singapore, reducing operating costs and allowing savings to be redirected to its youth development programmes. Since 2022, we have trained over 2,400 participants through our green capability building initiatives. Our green education programmes have reached over 600,000 people worldwide, strengthening energy and sustainability literacy. In 2025, Sembcorp contributed to the Institute of Technical Education Monthly Financial Assistance Scheme in Singapore, supporting approximately 700 students in pursuing their educational goals. We also launched the Sembcorp Energy League, which engaged more than 12,000 participants in 2025.
We will continue to focus on initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes and create sustainable, long-term benefits for the communities we serve. Health, Safety, Security and Environment While we celebrate our business achievements, the safety of our people remains important. We are deeply saddened by a contractor fatality that occurred in 2025. This incident reinforces the need for us to continue strengthening our safety culture and practices. We are strengthening our safety controls and processes, and enforcing the strictest adherence to contractor safety protocols across all sites. Beyond procedural improvements, we have also deployed proven AI-driven technologies to monitor work sites, allowing us to detect and deter unsafe acts. We remain resolute in our commitment to ensuring that every person who works with Sembcorp returns home safe every day. A Note of Thanks The resilience and success of Sembcorp are made possible by the dedication of our employees. We thank them for their professionalism and ability to adapt, innovate and execute in a complex environment. Message from the Chairman Dear Shareholders, After a long 50-year career spanning corporate and executive leadership, I have decided to retire as Chairman and step down from the board of Sembcorp with effect from June 1, 2026, in order to pursue my personal interests and passions.
Serving on the board since 2021 and as Chairman since 2023 has been a deeply rewarding and fulfilling journey. Funds borrowed by SFS are on-lent to businesses within the Group, where appropriate.
SFS employs an efficient cash management approach, recycling surplus cash from businesses within the Group to support areas with greater funding needs. Debt is managed through an ongoing and disciplined review of new and refinancing requirements to optimise the Group’s capital structure and allocation. Cash pooling structures established in various countries, maximise the use of available resources, channelling surplus funds from businesses to those with funding needs. We currently supply one-third of the power demand of data centres in Singapore, underscoring our role as a leading power partner to this fast-growing sector. Building on this momentum, Sembcorp continues to enhance earnings visibility by prioritising long-term contracting across the portfolio. In 2025, we secured over 120MW of new long-term PPAs with data centres as well as commercial and industrial customers, with tenures of five to 10 years. During the year, we also entered into a multi-service energy and utilities agreement with Aster Chemicals and Energy to provide integrated gas, power and utilities solutions for its refining and chemical complex in Pulau Bukom and Jurong Island, further expanding our portfolio of contracted energy solutions for industrial customers. In January 2026, we further strengthened our contracted position through a key terms agreement with Micron Semiconductor Asia Operations (Micron) to supply an additional 150MW of power. This expansion builds on the 18-year PPA signed in 2023, under which Sembcorp currently supplies up to 450MW to Micron’s Singapore facilities. The added capacity, which continues under the original term through 2041, supports Micron’s ongoing expansion and reinforces Sembcorp’s role as a trusted energy partner to Singapore’s energy-intensive industries. As of February 2026, 79% of our gas-fired power generation in Singapore1 was underpinned by long-term contracts, with 49% secured for over 10 years and 30% locked in for five to 10 years. In 2026, 5% of Sembcorp’s portfolio and approximately half of Senoko Energy’s portfolio will be re-contracted. We expect the prevailing softness in Singapore’s wholesale electricity market to exert downward pressure on tariffs, resulting in renewed contracts being signed at lower levels compared to prior periods. To strengthen our platform, we are also enhancing our generation capacity. In June 2025, we completed the acquisition of an additional 20% interest in Senoko Energy, bringing our effective interest to 50%. The enlarged ownership positions us to better serve the rising baseload demand from high-growth sectors including data centres and semiconductor manufacturing, while also unlocking operational and financial synergies with Senoko. It also enables a more carbon-efficient generation profile and delivers cost savings through portfolio optimisation, cost efficiency and cross-selling opportunities across both customer bases. We are also working to recontract or transition Senoko’s existing contracts into longer-tenure PPAs to strengthen earnings visibility. Construction of our new multi-utilities centre on Jurong Island, including a 600MW hydrogen-ready combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power plant, remains on track for completion in the fourth quarter of 2026. The high-efficiency, future-ready power plant will further enhance the fuel and cost efficiency of our fleet. It will also create growth headroom to support Singapore’s digital economy and manufacturing expansion. With this expanded multi-utilities platform, Sembcorp will continue to offer customers comprehensive and competitive energy and utilities solutions. Supporting Singapore’s Gas Supply Resilience In May 2025, a new fully government-owned entity, Singapore GasCo, was established to centralise the procurement and supply of natural gas to power generation companies in Singapore. Notwithstanding this structural change, Sembcorp’s gas portfolio in Singapore remains resilient and relevant. GasCo’s mandate does not extend to commercial and industrial customers, while our existing gas sales contracts with power generation companies are grandfathered. From a supply perspective, our gas portfolio is diversified across both piped natural gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG), with long-term LNG contracts secured until 2042.
Together with long-term gas procurement agreements and multi-year PPAs, these arrangements support reliable and competitively priced gas supply for customers, while contributing to Singapore’s broader objectives of energy security and price stability. Maintaining Earnings Visibility while Expanding Selectively Overseas Apart from Singapore, we continue to anchor our earnings through long-term contracts across overseas gas-fired assets. These include our gas-fired power plants in Bangladesh, Myanmar, Oman and the UAE. In Oman, we secured a new 10-year Power and Water Purchase Agreement for the Salalah Independent Water and Power Plant (IWPP), starting from April 2027. The renewed contract includes the continued supply of 465MW of power and 15 million imperial gallons of water per day, ensuring stable cash flows beyond the expiry of the current agreement. The renewal reinforces our strong partnership with Nama Power and Water Procurement Company and supports the long-term sustainability of our energy portfolio in the country. This is Sembcorp Industries' Annual Report for FY2025, covering the Singapore-based energy and urban solutions provider's financial performance, strategic initiatives, and corporate developments.

**FY2025 Financial Highlights:**
- Turnover: S$5,799m (down 10% from S$6,417m in 2024)
- Adjusted EBITDA: S$2,016m (down 2% from S$2,050m)
- Net profit before exceptional items and DPN FX: S$1,003m (vs S$1,014m in 2024)
- Reported net profit from continuing operations: S$984m (4% lower YoY)
- Return on Equity: 17.9% (2025), down from 20.1% in 2024
- Total dividend: 25.0 SG cents per share (up 9% from 23.0 cents in 2024), comprising interim 9.0 cents and proposed final dividend of 16.0 cents
- Earnings per share: 55.33 cents
- Net debt: S$7.8 billion (broadly unchanged)
- Gross debt: S$9.0 billion
- Operating cash flow: S$1.2 billion
- Owners' funds: S$5.5 billion
- Total assets: S$18,429 million
- Net assets per share: S$3.12
- Total shareholder return: 14%

**Segment Performance:**
- Gas and Related Services: Net profit before EI of S$701m (down 4%), contributing about 70% of Group earnings. Increased effective interest in Senoko Energy from 30% to 50% (additional 20% acquired in first half of 2025)
- Renewables: Net profit before EI of S$192m (up 5%), driven by better wind resources in India, full-year earnings from Vietnam subsidiaries, and new solar capacity
- Integrated Urban Solutions: Net profit before EI of S$178m (up 3%), supported by higher commercial and residential sales in Vietnam
- Decarbonisation Solutions: Net loss of S$23m

**Key Strategic Developments:**
- Completed divestment of Sembcorp Environment in March 2025 for S$383m inflow
- Proposed acquisition of Alinta Energy in Australia (announced December 2025) - immediately earnings accretive, providing entry into AAA-rated country with a potential pipeline of 10.4GW of renewables and firming development options
- 600MW hydrogen-ready CCGT power plant on Jurong Island on track for Q4 2026 completion

- Global energy portfolio of 28.5GW (8.1GW gas and others, 20.4GW renewables)
- Secured 20-year PPA for 125MW Dhofar II wind project in Oman (first wind project in the country)

- Awarded 86MWp Pandan Reservoir floating solar project in Singapore

- Three new VSIP projects awarded in Vietnam, bringing portfolio to 22 industrial parks across 15 provinces
- Signed MoU with NeutraDC for sustainable data centre infrastructure in Southeast Asia
- Secured new 10-year Power and Water Purchase Agreement in Oman (Salalah IWPP, 465MW power and 15 million imperial gallons of water per day)
- Signed key terms agreement with Micron (January 2026) to supply additional 150MW of power
- Supplies one-third of data centre power needs in Singapore
- In India, gross renewables capacity surpassed 7.6GW; secured 150MW firm and dispatchable renewable energy project from SJVN

- CEO: Wong Kim Yin

- Green capability building: 2,440 participants trained
- Green education: 604,200 participants engaged

European utilities prioritize cybersecurity, data privacy compliance with GDPR requirements, and integration with existing SCADA systems, leading to higher-value software and services offerings compared to other regions. The region's growth rate of **10.9%** CAGR through 2034 reflects mature market dynamics, replacement cycles for legacy systems, and investment in real-time monitoring capabilities across aging water infrastructure serving over 450 million urban residents across the continent.

The Middle East and Africa captured **6.1%** of global market value in 2025, with growth driven by critical water scarcity in the Middle East, expanding urban populations requiring improved water management, and international development initiatives supporting digital transformation across municipal water utilities in Sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa regions.

## Key Growth Drivers for Digital Twin in Water Networks 2025-2034

### Infrastructure Aging and Asset Management Requirements

Water distribution systems across developed nations operate beyond designed lifespan, with approximately **45%** of pipes in the United States exceeding 50 years old and experiencing failure rates of 2-3% annually in major metropolitan areas. Digital twin technologies enable utilities to model hydraulic conditions, predict component failures, prioritize rehabilitation investments, and extend asset lifecycles through data-driven maintenance strategies. **Siemens AG** reported that its digital twin solutions deployed across German water utilities have reduced unplanned outages by **34%** and extended pipe life by an average of **8-12 years** through optimized pressure management and predictive maintenance interventions. Municipal authorities in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific are allocating increasing capital budgets toward digital transformation initiatives addressing infrastructure renewal needs that require sophisticated asset management tools and real-time monitoring capabilities, directly stimulating market growth through 2034.

### Water Loss Reduction and Non-Revenue Water Management

Global non-revenue water losses represent approximately **$39 billion** in annual economic impact, with urban water utilities in developing nations experiencing losses ranging from **30-60%** due to aging infrastructure, illegal connections, and measurement inaccuracies. Digital twin platforms combined with IoT sensors, AI-powered anomaly detection, and hydraulic modeling enable utilities to pinpoint leakage locations, quantify losses by network segment, and implement targeted interventions reducing non-revenue water by **15-25%** within initial 2-3 year deployment periods. **TaKaDu** and **Ayyeka Technologies** have demonstrated that real-time monitoring combined with machine learning algorithms can identify emerging issues 30-60 days before physical failure, enabling proactive repairs that prevent catastrophic events and reduce water loss volumes. Water scarcity conditions across Asia Pacific, Middle East, and parts of Europe have made non-revenue water reduction a critical strategic priority for utilities seeking operational efficiency gains and enhanced service reliability, driving sustained digital twin adoption and technology investment through forecast period.

### Regulatory Compliance and Environmental Mandates

European Union directives, including the Water Framework Directive, Drinking Water Directive, and emerging Digital Operational Resilience Act provisions, mandate enhanced monitoring, reporting, and cybersecurity compliance for water utilities managing critical infrastructure. The United States EPA's Lead and Copper Rule revisions require utilities to implement real-time quality monitoring and predictive analytics for corrosion control, directly creating demand for digital twin platforms with advanced water quality simulation capabilities and multi-parameter tracking across distribution networks. Regulatory bodies across APAC, including China's Ministry of Water Resources and India's central water commission, are increasingly mandating digital asset registers, real-time network monitoring systems, and integrated water resource management platforms that incorporate digital twin functionalities. **Bentley Systems** and **AVEVA Group** have aligned product developments with emerging regulatory requirements, enabling utilities to achieve compliance through integrated monitoring, reporting, and predictive maintenance capabilities embedded within digital twin ecosystems. These regulatory drivers create sustained pressure for technology adoption and system upgrades among utilities seeking to demonstrate compliance, manage liability risks, and optimize operational efficiency within evolving regulatory frameworks through 2034.

### IoT Sensor Proliferation and Real-Time Data Availability

The cost of industrial IoT sensors has declined by approximately **60-70%** since 2019, enabling utilities to deploy thousands of pressure, flow, and quality sensors across distribution networks at economically viable capital costs previously prohibitive for municipal budgets. 5G network expansion across developed and emerging markets is enabling real-time data transmission from remote field sensors to central digital twin platforms with sub-second latency, supporting responsive control algorithms and emergency response capabilities previously impossible with legacy communication infrastructure. **Grundfos** and **Xylem Inc.** have integrated IoT sensor technologies into pump station equipment, enabling continuous performance monitoring, predictive maintenance alerts, and optimization recommendations that enhance operational efficiency and extend equipment lifespans. The proliferation of cloud computing infrastructure and edge computing nodes has reduced capital barriers for utilities seeking to implement digital twin solutions, enabling scaled deployments across networks of varying sizes and complexity. This technology foundation supports rapid expansion of digital twin adoption across geographic regions and utility categories, driving market growth through increased implementation rates and expansion of existing deployments across larger network segments through forecast period.

## What is the impact of digital twin technology on reducing non-revenue water in municipal systems?

Digital twin platforms combined with IoT sensors can identify leakage locations within **48-72 hours** of occurrence compared to **30-60 days** for traditional inspection methods, enabling utilities to reduce non-revenue water losses by **15-25%** within initial deployment phases. Real-time hydraulic modeling allows utilities to optimize pressure settings across network segments, reducing stress on aging pipes and preventing cascade failures that account for significant portions of non-revenue water in developing world cities. Utilities deploying **Innovyze** and **IBM** digital twin solutions have reported achieving non-revenue water reduction targets within **18-24 months** of full implementation, delivering cost savings of $2-5 million annually for utilities serving 500,000+ residents.

## Digital Twin for Water Network Market by Component 2025-2034

The component segment demonstrates clear market stratification with software solutions commanding the largest share at **$1.18 billion** in 2025, representing **42.3%** of total market value and reflecting the critical role of data analytics, modeling engines, and user interfaces in digital twin value delivery. Software platforms integrate hydraulic simulation capabilities, real-time data visualization dashboards, predictive analytics modules, and integration layers connecting to existing SCADA, GIS, and enterprise systems within water utilities. **Bentley Systems**' OpenFlows product suite and **Innovyze**' InfoWorks ICM platform dominate enterprise software markets, offering comprehensive hydraulic modeling, network analysis, and optimization capabilities that enable utilities to plan infrastructure investments, test operational scenarios, and validate design modifications before implementation. Advanced software incorporates AI and machine learning algorithms for anomaly detection, demand forecasting, and pump station optimization that continuously improve operational efficiency without human intervention. The software segment is experiencing accelerating adoption driven by cloud-based deployment models that reduce capital expenditure requirements, enable rapid scaling across multiple facilities, and facilitate integration with IoT sensor networks and advanced analytics platforms. Growing emphasis on cybersecurity, regulatory compliance automation, and mobile workforce enablement is driving software feature expansion and premium pricing models that support **14.7%** CAGR forecast for software through 2034, outpacing overall market growth.

Services segment captured **35.1%** market share representing **$0.98 billion** in 2025, encompassing implementation, integration, customization, training, and ongoing technical support required for successful digital twin deployment and operation. System integrators and consulting firms specializing in water utility transformation have become critical service providers, with **Suez Water Technologies & Solutions**, **Veolia Water Technologies**, and **Royal HaskoningDHV** offering end-to-end implementation services combining technology deployment, change management, and staff training programs. Implementation services typically account for **30-50%** of total deployment costs for enterprise-scale digital twin initiatives, reflecting complexity of integrating digital platforms with existing utility infrastructure, legacy systems, and organizational processes spanning engineering, operations, and customer service functions. Professional services demand is expanding as utilities recognize that technology adoption alone is insufficient without organizational change management, staff training, and process reengineering support required for realizing digital twin benefits. The services segment is forecasted to grow at **11.2%** CAGR through 2034 as digital twin implementations mature, requiring ongoing optimization services, staff augmentation, and platform evolution consulting to maintain competitive advantage and operational performance.

Hardware segment including sensors, edge computing devices, and specialized monitoring equipment comprised **22.6%** market share at **$0.63 billion** in 2025, with growth driven by expanding sensor deployments across water distribution networks and treatment facilities. Industrial-grade pressure sensors, flow meters, water quality analyzers, and acoustic leak detection hardware have become essential infrastructure components enabling digital twin systems to function effectively. **Ayyeka Technologies** specializes in smart sensor solutions for water networks, deploying devices that transmit data via multiple connectivity options including cellular, satellite, and Wi-Fi networks to accommodate diverse deployment environments across urban and remote areas. Edge computing devices and local data processing nodes are increasingly deployed at critical network junctures and treatment facilities, enabling low-latency analytics and automated control functions without continuous cloud connectivity dependencies. The hardware segment is projected to expand at **10.8%** CAGR through 2034 as utilities increase sensor densification to achieve more granular network visibility, deploy specialized hardware for water quality monitoring to address emerging contaminant concerns, and implement redundant sensing infrastructure supporting critical operational decisions.

![Global Digital Twin For Water Network Market Share by Segment Doughnut Chart](https://dataintelo.com/assets/images/charts/680281/segment-share.svg)

## Digital Twin for Water Network Market by Application 2025-2034

Asset management emerged as the leading application capturing **24.8%** market share in 2025, driven by critical need for utilities to optimize capital spending on aging infrastructure replacement and rehabilitation programs. Digital twin platforms enable utilities to develop comprehensive asset registers, model hydraulic impacts of infrastructure changes, prioritize rehabilitation investments based on failure risk assessment, and validate design modifications before costly capital projects. **Bentley Systems**' digital twin solutions facilitate asset lifecycle management by modeling infrastructure performance across multiple scenarios, enabling utilities to identify optimal timing for pipe replacement, pump refurbishment, and treatment facility upgrades that maximize asset value while maintaining service reliability. Utilities are investing in asset management digital twins to reduce emergency repairs by **25-40%** and extend infrastructure asset lifecycles by **8-15 years**, generating return on investment within **3-5 years** for typical municipal systems. The asset management application is supporting adoption across water utilities of all sizes, with particular emphasis in regions with aging infrastructure including North America, Europe, and parts of Asia Pacific experiencing rapid infrastructure aging.

Network monitoring applications represented **21.3%** market share in 2025, encompassing real-time visibility into flow, pressure, quality parameters, and operational status across distribution networks. Digital twin platforms integrated with SCADA systems provide continuous monitoring of network performance, enabling operators to detect emerging issues, optimize pump operations, and respond to disruptions within minutes rather than hours or days. Real-time monitoring capabilities support emergency response coordination, enabling utilities to isolate contamination events, manage pressure fluctuations, and maintain service continuity during disruption events. **Siemens AG** has deployed networked monitoring solutions across major European water utilities, delivering real-time visibility into thousands of network parameters simultaneously and enabling predictive interventions that prevent service disruptions. The network monitoring application is growing at **12.8%** CAGR as utilities expand sensor networks, increasing connectivity and data availability enabling more sophisticated real-time analytics and responsive control capabilities.

## How do digital twin solutions improve leak detection compared to traditional methods?

Digital twin platforms combined with acoustic sensors and AI algorithms can detect emerging leaks within **24-48 hours** of occurrence, compared to **30-90 days** for traditional inspection methods, enabling utilities to respond rapidly and minimize water loss. Real-time pressure and flow analysis within digital twin models can pinpoint leak locations to within **50-100 meters** of actual occurrence, significantly reducing excavation and inspection costs compared to manual field surveys. **TaKaDu** and **Ayyeka** digital twin solutions leverage machine learning algorithms that analyze historical patterns and real-time data to forecast emerging leaks **30-60 days** in advance, enabling preventive interventions before catastrophic failures occur.

Leak detection applications accounted for **18.4%** market share in 2025, reflecting strong demand for technologies addressing non-revenue water losses and enabling rapid response to pipe failures. Digital twin platforms with integrated acoustic monitoring, pressure transient analysis, and AI-powered anomaly detection can identify leakage locations with unprecedented speed and accuracy, enabling utilities to prioritize response efforts and minimize water loss. **Innovyze**' transient modeling capabilities and **TaKaDu**' machine learning algorithms have demonstrated **85-95%** accuracy in leak detection when integrated with comprehensive sensor networks, enabling utilities to achieve cost-effective leak detection without expensive manual inspections. The leak detection application is expanding across developing world utilities experiencing high non-revenue water losses, creating strong demand for cost-effective solutions addressing critical operational challenges.

Predictive maintenance applications captured **16.9%** market share in 2025, leveraging digital twin capabilities to forecast equipment failures and schedule maintenance activities before breakdowns occur. Pump stations, treatment facilities, and control systems can be continuously monitored through digital twins that model operational parameters, detect performance degradation, and alert maintenance teams to imminent failures. **Grundfos** and **Xylem** have integrated predictive maintenance capabilities into pump equipment, enabling remote monitoring and failure forecasting that supports proactive maintenance scheduling. The predictive maintenance application enables utilities to reduce emergency repairs by **35-50%** and extend equipment lifecycles while improving operational reliability and reducing costs associated with unplanned outages. Growth in predictive maintenance applications is supported by expanding IoT sensor deployments, cloud computing infrastructure, and artificial intelligence capabilities enabling increasingly sophisticated failure prediction models.

Network optimization applications represented **11.8%** market share in 2025, enabling utilities to model operational scenarios, optimize pump operations, and improve energy efficiency across distribution networks. Digital twin platforms simulate impacts of operational changes including pump scheduling adjustments, valve position modifications, and treatment process refinements, enabling utilities to identify optimization opportunities that reduce energy consumption and operating costs. **Bentley Systems** and **Innovyze** optimization modules enable utilities to identify energy savings of **10-20%** through hydraulic optimization and pump operation fine-tuning, delivering cost reductions that support technology investment returns. The optimization application is expanding as utilities prioritize energy efficiency, reduce carbon footprint, and optimize treatment processes to meet emerging water quality standards and sustainability objectives. Other applications including demand forecasting, water quality modeling, and customer engagement captured **6.8%** market share, with growth driven by expanding utility priorities and emerging digital twin capabilities supporting secondary applications beyond primary focus areas.

## Digital Twin for Water Network Market by Deployment Mode 2025-2034

Cloud deployment emerged as the dominant mode capturing **62.4%** market share in 2025, reflecting utilities' preference for reduced capital expenditure, scalable infrastructure, and reduced IT complexity associated with cloud-based digital twin platforms. Cloud deployment models enable utilities to access enterprise-class software capabilities without substantial upfront capital investment, supporting rapid scaling across multiple facilities and geographic locations. **Innovyze**', **IBM**, and **Schneider Electric** offer cloud-native digital twin platforms supporting multi-tenant architectures that reduce per-user costs and enable rapid feature deployment and security updates. Cloud platforms provide superior disaster recovery capabilities, geographic redundancy, and automated backup systems that support business continuity during disruption events. Security concerns have been substantially addressed through implementation of encryption, authentication protocols, and compliance certifications including ISO 27001 and FedRAMP that enable utilities to deploy mission-critical systems within cloud environments. The cloud deployment segment is growing at **14.2%** CAGR through 2034 as utilities migrate from legacy on-premises infrastructure, embrace cloud-native architectures, and adopt multi-cloud strategies supporting operational flexibility and reduced vendor lock-in risks.

On-premises deployment maintained **37.6%** market share in 2025, preferred by utilities with specific cybersecurity requirements, legacy system dependencies, or limited cloud connectivity in remote service areas. On-premises solutions provide utilities with direct control over data, infrastructure, and operational systems, addressing concerns regarding data sovereignty and regulatory compliance in certain jurisdictions. **Bentley Systems**, **AVEVA Group**, and **Siemens AG** continue supporting on-premises deployment options for enterprise utilities requiring deep system integration with existing SCADA, GIS, and corporate IT infrastructure. Hybrid deployment approaches combining on-premises systems for operational technology with cloud-based analytics and visualization platforms are increasingly adopted by utilities seeking flexibility and risk mitigation across digital twin implementations. The on-premises segment is projected to decline slightly to **35.8%** market share by 2034, though absolute revenue growth of **9.6%** CAGR reflects ongoing demand from utilities with specific operational or regulatory requirements supporting on-premises architectures. Investment patterns show utilities increasingly adopting hybrid deployment models leveraging on-premises operational technology with cloud-based analytics, business intelligence, and collaboration capabilities supporting enhanced flexibility and reduced total cost of ownership.

## What are the main differences between cloud and on-premises digital twin deployment for water utilities?

Cloud deployments reduce capital expenditure by **60-75%** compared to on-premises solutions and offer superior scalability, **99.99%** availability guarantees, and automated security updates. On-premises deployments provide direct data control, support legacy system integration, and address cybersecurity concerns in jurisdictions restricting data movement, though requiring higher capital investment and IT staffing. Hybrid approaches combining on-premises operational technology with cloud-based analytics are increasingly adopted, representing approximately **28%** of new digital twin deployments by **2026**.

## Digital Twin for Water Network Market by End-User 2025-2034

Municipal water utilities dominated end-user segment with **58.6%** market share in 2025, representing the largest customer category for digital twin technologies addressing infrastructure challenges across urban water distribution systems. "We make investment decisions based on the potential value to Autodesk and to our customers, and increasingly, we give significant consideration to an investment's impact on sustainability, as we did with our [Spacemaker acquisition](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=3114107-1&h=3596746620&u=https%3A%2F%2Fadsknews.autodesk.com%2Fpressrelease%2Fautodesk-completes-acquisition-of-spacemaker-provider-of-ai-and-generative-design-enabled-urban-design-platform&a=Spacemaker+acquisition) last year," said Andrew Anagnost, CEO and president of Autodesk. "Innovyze is no different. Responsibly managing our use of water runs parallel to successfully sustaining life. Together, these capabilities allow civil engineers, water utility companies, plant operators and water experts the ability to better respond to issues before they become emergencies and to improve planning for the future.

"Water is life, and safely and sustainably managing water from cloud to ocean has been Innovyze's mission for more than thirty years," said Colby Manwaring, CEO of Innovyze. "Autodesk and Innovyze's technologies could not be more complementary, which will accelerate our shared vision for improving our resilience to climate change and quality of life for all communities."

![](https://aecmag.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/mart-BW-65x65.jpg)Posted on [February 24, 2021 at March 9, 2021](https://aecmag.com/civil-engineering/autodesk-acquires-water-modelling-firm-innovyze-for-1-billion/) by [Martyn Day](https://aecmag.com/author/martyn/)

### Autodesk buys Portland-based Innovyze for $1 Billion, to enter smart water infrastructure modelling market

---

In its first acquisition of the year, Autodesk has spent $1 billion cash on Portland OR based developer [Innovyze](https://www.innovyze.com/en-us). The 35 year-old software company is a specialist in smart water infrastructure modelling, simulation, and predictive analyses technologies. 

According to Autodesk this acquisition helps it “to provide end-to-end solutions for design, construction, and now, operations of water infrastructure, enabling them to accelerate sustainable outcomes and help communities build resilience for the future.”

Innovyze’s modelling, simulation, and predictive analyses solutions enable cost-effective and sustainable water distribution networks, water collection systems, water and wastewater treatment plants, and flood protection systems. Further, Innovyze’s solutions centralise infrastructure asset visibility to optimise capital and operational expenses.

Autodesk stated that “combining Innovyze’s portfolio with its own design and analysis solutions, including Autodesk Civil 3D, Autodesk InfraWorks, and the [Autodesk Construction Cloud,](https://construction.autodesk.com) offers civil engineers, water utility companies and water experts the ability to better respond to issues and to improve planning.”

### Executive comments

“We can achieve a more sustainable planet, but we can’t do it without responsibly managing our use of water and securing its future,” said Andrew Anagnost, Autodesk president and CEO. “An estimated $1.9 trillion is required to address global water infrastructure needs by 2030, and by fundamentally changing the way systems are designed, constructed, and operated, we are best positioned to overcome this challenge and realize the better world we’ve imagined.”

“Nearly nine trillion gallons of water are lost each year worldwide due to prolonged leaks and pipe breaks, but we cannot manage or fix what we cannot see,” said Amy Bunszel, executive vice president, AEC Design Solutions at Autodesk. “Innovyze’s portfolio of operational analytics, distribution modelling, and asset management solutions provides the insight needed to identify this and other potential problems before they become a crisis.”

“For thirty-five years Innovyze has been a hidden part of the daily lives of millions of people around the world, helping to deliver fresh, clean water, managing sewage and flooding in our communities, and turning wastewater into safe water,” said Colby Manwaring, CEO of Innovyze.

“Similarly, if you look at the built world around us, Autodesk’s design DNA is found in just about every structure you see above ground and below, so it makes strategic sense to bring together our complementary organizations critical to much of the world’s population. We look forward to completing the acquisition and getting to work, together.”

### AEC Magazine thoughts on Innovyze acquisition

By any measurement, this is the biggest deal so far under CEO Andrew Anagnost. Since 2017 Autodesk had already spent $2.4 billion acquiring firms and technologies predominantly for its construction cloud play. Innovyze appears to be a much more strategic purchase, with regards to entering deeper into the Civils space, targeting specifically water. 

In Autodesk’s justification slide deck, it states that Innovyze’s lets it better address $1.7B total addressable market. Mainly due to the fact that Innovyze is the largest pure-play global water infrastructure software provider with regulatory stamp of approval. The company has 240 employees and is conveniently located in Portland Oregon, which is also the home of Autodesk’s mechanical CAD division.

To date, Autodesk’s presence in infrastructure and plant, has tended to less than market dominating. Autodesk feels it has the building space, but has tough competition in transport roads, plant, rail and water, against players such as [Hexagon](https://hexagon.com/about/divisions/ppm), [Trimble](https://buildings.trimble.com) and [Bentley Systems](https://www.bentley.com/en).

Autodesk’s intentions now go beyond competing in the design offering space, as it looks to build a compelling, cloud-based, digital twin business. This acquisition of Innovyze takes the companies relevance from design and construction all the way through to operation and decommission. While Autodesk has the potential to democratise digital twins in the building space, it’s lack of dominance in the infrastructure market is an issue.

Autodesk’s digital twin technologies are also still embryonic, with [Autodesk Tandem](https://aecmag.com/digital-twin/public-beta-for-autodesk-tandem-digital-twin-platform/), now in public beta, and yet to be released. Clearly Autodesk is not going to stop at building digital twins of above-ground installations, but wants to also document what goes on under our feet. However, to do this it has a fight on its hands with the incumbent competition to win market share.

While Autodesk has now spent $3.4 billion acquiring firms in the last three years, we are not sure how this news will be received by Revit customers who have been [complaining of lack of development and increased cost of ownership](https://aecmag.com/bim/autodesk-aec-customers-demand-better-value/). While Autodesk has promised to re-double its efforts on delivering a broader three-year roadmap for Revit, it seems to prefer to spend much more money on acquiring firms for its construction cloud and now digital twin/ civil engineering play.

This is a news article from AEC Magazine (aecmag.com) reporting that Autodesk acquired Portland, Oregon-based water modelling firm Innovyze for $1 billion in cash. This was Autodesk's first acquisition of 2021 (published February 24, 2021) and was aimed at entering the smart water infrastructure modelling market.

Key facts:
- Innovyze is a 35-year-old software company specializing in smart water infrastructure modelling, simulation, and predictive analysis technologies.
- The acquisition enables Autodesk to provide end-to-end solutions for design, construction, and operations of water infrastructure.
- Innovyze's solutions cover water distribution networks, water collection systems, water and wastewater treatment plants, and flood protection systems.
- The deal will combine Innovyze's portfolio with Autodesk Civil 3D, Autodesk InfraWorks, and Autodesk Construction Cloud.
- Innovyze has 240 employees and is located in Portland, Oregon (also home to Autodesk's mechanical CAD division).
- Autodesk had already spent $2.4 billion on acquisitions since 2017 (predominantly for its construction cloud play), bringing total spend to $3.4 billion in the last three years.
- Autodesk's justification cites that the acquisition helps it address a $1.7B total addressable market, as Innovyze is the largest pure-play global water infrastructure software provider.
- The article notes this is the biggest deal under CEO Andrew Anagnost and that Autodesk's digital twin technologies (Autodesk Tandem) are still in public beta.
- Autodesk faces competition in the infrastructure space from Hexagon, Trimble, and Bentley Systems.
- The article raises concerns that Revit customers have been complaining about lack of development and increased cost of ownership, while Autodesk spends heavily on acquisitions.

Executive quotes are included from Andrew Anagnost (Autodesk president and CEO), Amy Bunszel (EVP, AEC Design Solutions), and Colby Manwaring (CEO of Innovyze).
args.key_excerpts: "An estimated $1.9 trillion is required to address global water infrastructure needs by 2030, and by fundamentally changing the way systems are designed, constructed, and operated, we are best positioned to overcome this challenge and realize the better world we've imagined." - Andrew Anagnost, Autodesk president and CEO

## WATER DIGITAL TWIN

# Digital twins in the water industry

Learn how digital twins for water and wastewater networks and treatment plants help utilities simulate events, optimize performance, and help streamline regulatory reporting.

[Learn about Info360 Insight](https://www.autodesk.com/products/info360-insight/overview)[Explore the water industry](https://www.autodesk.com/industry/water)

![Image 1: What are digital twins for water utilities? Feature Image](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/3Tox7O3M5mUpGOq2qFK2p5/7ca774483eaae282939ece343c781c82/digitaltwinswaterutilitywhataredigitaltwins1172x660.jpg)

Digital twins are virtual representations of physical water system assets.

### What are digital twins for water utilities?

[Digital twins](https://intandem.autodesk.com/about-digital-twins/) for water utilities are virtual representations of physical water system assets that integrate data, models, and analytics to run simulations using hydraulic models, machine learning, and artificial intelligence.

### How digital twins work in water utility management

Digital twins work by integrating sensor data and [hydraulic models](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water/hydraulic-modeling.html) of water and wastewater systems to simulate and predict performance under changing conditions, improving the management of facilities and water assets.

![Image 2: How digital twins work in water utility management Feature Image](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/1sFIiKMtObTbNtFjjF2J3s/24e722a15c821bca120424053d27f59d/how-digital-twins-work-in-water-utility-management-1172x660.jpg)

Digital twins simulate asset performance in various conditions.

## How digital twins aid decision making

Digital twins for water utilities can help with decision making on many levels.

![Image 3: A digital model highlights a colorful rendering of a neighborhood with areas of concern for flooding outlined in black.](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/KtaOYyh1npDgVRXyTIKhp/91751fd8ac4edadc7c276c893084f3d5/planning-for-the-future-thumb-788x444.jpg)

# Planning for the future

The type of data you put into your digital twin for water-based simulation will determine whether it’s best suited for long-term, short-term, or immediate decision making—or even all three.

![Image 4: Two individuals in hard hats examine data on a computer screen, in an industrial setting.](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/6mJR7zRGBNRijOxDo7iRLL/0c378fe98b0bb35c058510922868b8a1/predicting-behavior-thumb-788x444.jpg)

# Predicting behavior

By creating a virtual model of the system, you can take steps to predict the behavior of components within that system, and your infrastructure as a whole.

![Image 5: A water utility worker surveys a wastewater treatment plant with a tablet.](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/2IHZ7zzAj4r7LiR2J0JCNF/fe518ee5937703f434aeeffa2cd6bed4/digitaltwinswaterutilitymanagementmonitoring788x444.jpg)

# Monitoring

Cloud-based monitoring helps you keep track of what’s happening right now, while digital twin water simulations can give you the intel you need to plan ahead.

## Software for water utility digital twins

## Info360 Insight

Real-time operational performance analytics, modeling, and alerting tools in the cloud

[Product details](https://www.autodesk.com/products/info360-insight/overview)

## InfoWorks ICM

Model complex hydraulic and hydrologic network elements quickly, accurately, and collaboratively.

[Product details](https://www.autodesk.com/products/infoworks-icm/overview)

## InfoWorks WS Pro

Comprehensive and collaborative water distribution analysis and modeling

[Product details](https://www.autodesk.com/products/infoworks-ws-pro/overview)

## Benefits of water utility digital twins

### Real-time monitoring

Monitor and analyze water assets with cloud-based monitoring.

### Predictive maintenance

Use water infrastructure digital twins to run simulations and analysis for asset repairs to reduce costs.

### Operations optimization

Manage procedures for faster resolution of operational incidents in water management.

### Compliance reporting

Visualize network data to meet regulatory requirements for reporting.

## What are the first steps toward making a digital twin?

Digital twins in the water industry are useful for many reasons, but it’s important to set priorities specific to your operation when creating one.

### Decide your goals

Begin by identifying what your goals are, and make sure they’re actionable.

### Make a plan

Figure out what data and metrics you require to meet your goals, and how these can be put in place.

### Implement your plan

Once you understand these priorities, you can move forward with your implementation of a water digital twin. Your specialists and data scientists can better approach the task using software such as Autodesk[Info360 Insight](https://www.autodesk.com/products/info360-insight/overview).

![Image 6: How a digital twin can help water utilities plan ahead Feature Image](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/5Y6vdnLxvRW4iEihl7Fi0j/59d31af3995e6d74845604ade9861c84/how-a-digital-twin-can-help-water-utilities-plan-ahead-1172x660.jpg)

Digital twins are helping global firm Veolia Water Technologies improve flood modeling.

### How a digital twin can help water utilities plan ahead

Many water utilities have a large amount of data about their operations and they don’t even know it, let alone have the capability to leverage it for decision making and planning. Well-planned digital twins for water utilities can bring all that data together from different sensors, teams, and reports into one central hub accessible by all who need it within the organization. Autodesk’s hydraulic modeling[software](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water/hydraulic-modeling.html)will also help create powerful in-depth simulations so you can make decisions with actionable foresight.

## How are water digital twins being used?

![Image 7: An aerial photo shows canals running through Glasgow.](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/5d5OdQZ0ng2IZCUZAHfSTv/9be6632220ab307f509d8c58599e62f5/dt-scottishcanals788x444.png)

[Read story](https://www.autodesk.com/customer-stories/glasgow-smart-canal)

[Read story](https://blogs.autodesk.com/innovyze/2023/02/28/extraordinary-flood-mapping-project-influencing-the-way-we-prepare-for-floods-in-australia/)

[Read story](https://www.autodesk.com/customer-stories/stantec-wellington-water)

### Digital twins in the water industry and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT)

In an increasingly connected world, every piece of hardware can be a data point. The [Industrial Internet of Things](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/solutions/industrial-internet-of-things.html) (IIoT)—the networking of sensors, actuators, and other components—means that data can be effortlessly brought into your water utility’s digital twin to create a computerized representation of the infrastructure and equipment. This real-time data, combined with powerful hydraulic modeling techniques, gives you the power to see what’s really going on across systems at all times, from wherever you are.

![Image 11: Digital twins in the water industry and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) Feature Image](https://images.ctfassets.net/v7wr16nrr0mz/4IUgpKPjAdiQdZk0cvI1eV/4a23865003fef767523bf930edf27e7a/digital-twins-in-the-water-industry-and-the-industrial-internet-of-things-iiot-1172x660.jpg)

Networked IIoT sensors provide real-time data about water utility performance.

Autodesk experts and customers prepare Australian [water infrastructure](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water.html) for the 2032 Olympics with digital twin solutions for stormwater networks.

## Frequently asked questions (FAQ) about water utility digital twins

### ### What is water digitalization?

Water digitalization describes the use of digital technologies to improve water management and operations. It can help utilities become more resilient, innovative, efficient, and sustainable. This includes the use of technologies such as sensor and data analytics, artificial intelligence simulations, digital twins for water management, smart meters, and mobile apps.

### ### What problems do digital twins solve?

Digital twins solve various problems for [water industry](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water.html) professionals, such as:

*   Improving system performance and reliability by monitoring and optimizing network operations

*   Enhancing system resilience and adaptability by simulating and testing scenarios

*   Reducing costs and risks by identifying and preventing potential water asset failures and disruptions

*   Increasing customer satisfaction and engagement by providing real-time feedback and transparency with robust reporting

### ### How can water digital twins improve productivity?

Water digital twins can improve productivity by:

*   Delivering real-time information, analysis, and insights on infrastructure performance

*   Enabling operational efficiency and accuracy using simulations to make data-backed decisions

*   Reducing operational costs and risks by preventing asset failures and disruptions

*   Improving customer service by providing transparency and maximizing uptime

See more FAQ

See less FAQ

⌄

### ### What are other new technologies in the water sector?

Other emerging technologies in the [water utility sector](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water.html) that aid in the digital transformation include:

*   Smart meters and sensors that collect and transmit real-time data on water quality, consumption, pressure, and leakage

*   Cloud computing and big data analytics that store and process large volumes of data

*   Artificial intelligence and machine learning that enable predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, demand forecasting, and customer service

### ### What are some considerations when adopting digital twins in water utility management?

Some considerations when adopting digital twins in [water utility management](https://www.autodesk.com/content/autodesk/global/en/industry/water.html) are:

*   The data quality and integration of sources and formats across various water infrastructure assets

*   The scalability and flexibility of the digital twin platform to handle complex and dynamic water systems

*   The security and privacy of sensitive data and information

*   The cost-benefit analysis and ROI of investing in water digital twin technology versus traditional methods of operational management

This is a presentation from Autodesk University 2022 (September 27-29, 2022, New Orleans) delivered by Ryan Brown, PE, Technical Solutions Engineer at Autodesk, titled "Digital Twin: Is it Just a Buzzword?" The presentation unpacks the concept of digital twins in the water/wastewater infrastructure sector.

**Key Topics Covered:**

1. **Definition of Digital Twin**: A digital twin can be used for monitoring, diagnostics, and prognostics to optimize asset performance and utilization. Sensory data combined with physics-based models improves prognostics outcomes. The SWAN (Smart Water Networks) Forum defines it as "a dynamic digital representation of real-world entity(s) and their behaviors, using models with static and dynamic data that enable insights and interactions to drive actionable and improved outcomes."

2. **Asset Management (6-Part Breakdown)**: The presentation outlines a framework covering infrastructure (what you own and where), inspections/surveys (condition and remaining life), incidents (how the network is performing/failing), inhabitants & investors (services delivered to customers), investments (where to spend first dollars), and interventions & remediations (how to improve performance).

3. **Autodesk/Innovyze Product Solutions**:
   - **Info360 Asset**: Leverages asset condition data (CCTV inspections, GIS, hydraulic models, asset inventory, work history, ML failure prediction, risk analysis) for capital planning, budget optimization, and SSO prevention.
   - **Info360 Insight**: Leverages data investments for asset management, model calibration, and water loss reduction. Features include real-time analytics, hydraulic model integration, dashboarding/KPIs, incident management, alert management, workflow automation, sensor health, and system forecasting.

4. **Live Modeling System Requirements**: A continuous system that harvests/checks/screens live data, forecasts whole system at regular intervals, stitches together continuous simulation, provides realistic system representation, translates results into intelligence, and processes output and raw data together. Key components include a hydraulic model, sensor network, SCADA/telemetry, radar, simulation server, and time-series database. Data challenges include gaps, spikes, anomalies, data conversions, smoothing, and sensor aggregation.

5. **Case Studies**:
   - **North Charleston Sewer District**: Used Info360 Asset with decision tree analysis and pipe inspection QA/QC to streamline CIP (Capital Improvement Program) proposal process. Outcome: multi-million-dollar plans approved by the Board of Commissioners "with no questions asked" due to transparency. Challenges addressed included communicating decision factors to stakeholders and integrating diverse data types (CMMS, CCTV, GIS, Excel).
   - **Glasgow Smart Canals Project**: Used live modeling twin with RTC (Real-Time Control) to optimize sluice gate controls, maintaining appropriate water surface to mitigate flooding while allowing boat navigation. Outcome: level optimization enabled up to 2 million cubic feet of additional storage and 270 acres of land became accessible for development.
   - **Anglian Water**: Automated nightly model builds from GIS data with scripting, with constant model validation against real-time SCADA data. Service area covers 5 million customers. Outcome: modelers could focus on analysis rather than data management.

6. **Relation to Federal Legislation (IIJA Bill)**:
   - Drinking Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Act (S. 914): Sec. 112 (advanced drinking water technologies for small systems), Sec. 213 (water data sharing pilot program/cloud), Sec. 219 (advanced clean water technologies study/cybersecurity).
   - Water Quality Protection and Job Creation Act of 2021 (H.R. 1915): Sec. 11 (smart wastewater infrastructure technology grant program/AI).
   - The Innovyze Digital AMP platform can provide "collateral" for Federal, State, and Local funding, supporting grant applications.

KEY FINDINGS ON THE WATER UTILITIES INDUSTRY:

1. **Current Status**: China's water utilities industry has entered a high-quality development stage. In 2024, total national water usage was stable at 592.8 billion cubic meters. **Drivers for Digital Water Development:**
- Internal drivers: high-quality drinking water requirements, environmental compliance standards, urban safety and resilience, low-carbon green development, shift from experience-based management, low operational efficiency, established information systems, and growing digital awareness.
- External drivers: policy, technology, economy, and demand.

**Current Status of Digital Water in China:**
- A 2017-2020 survey of 194 representative water enterprises showed widespread attention and high value recognition for digital water construction.
- China's digital water construction is transitioning from automation and informatization toward smart/intelligent development.
- Water supply enterprises focus information systems on customer service (billing, WeChat public accounts, installation management); drainage enterprises focus on operational control (automation, water quality online monitoring, central control systems).
- Goals include unmanned water plant regulation, scientific pipeline network dispatch, and efficient process control.
- Half of surveyed enterprises have established independent digital management departments; leading enterprises are characterized by strong leadership attention and deep business department involvement.
- Digital management departments are transitioning toward strategic support functions, integrating IT with business applications, and emphasizing "top-leader projects."
- Government digital water procurement projects are concentrated in southeastern and central China.
- Future 5-year investment forecasts show polarized investment trends overall, particularly in central and north China regions and for smaller enterprises (under 500,000 tons); enterprises over 500,000 tons show more balanced investment.
- China's digital water research emphasizes application and practical water issues (water quality monitoring, pollution control), while Europe and the US focus more on theory and method innovation (big data model/algorithm development). China has 95 national-level research projects related to "smart + water."
- Chinese digital water algorithms focus on AI-based watershed pollution tracing and risk prediction.

Products include smart manhole covers, smart pumps, smart valves, smart water pillars, hydraulic control equipment, and grid-based waterlogging recognition systems. **Development Trends and Problems:**
Three urgent needs: (1) improved cognition of digitalization at the leadership level; (2) coordinated, unified construction and industry-recognized digital water standards (avoiding fragmented "each fighting for themselves"); (3) specialized digital water talent (universities lack relevant courses). --- SOURCE 1: Interview: digital trends in the Chinese water market | Aquatech ---
URL: https://www.aquatechtrade.com/water-stories/water-treatment/china-ai-digital-water-market-challenges-opportunties

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article is an interview with Bruno Lhopiteau, managing director of Siveco China and Bluebee Tech, about digital trends in the Chinese water market. Published by Aquatech Online on Tuesday, 23 September 2025.

Key findings from the interview:

- China is among the world's fastest adopters of digital tools in the water sector, driven by government mandates like the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-2025). By 2024, more than 90% of urban water utilities adopted 'basic' IoT sensors for real-time monitoring. The 'Digital Water' initiative post-2020 led to Smart Water solutions in 70% of new wastewater treatment plants for predictive maintenance and leak detection. Investments exceed €10 billion annually, outpacing global averages (around 40% in Europe per IWA reports).

- Despite impressive statistics, Lhopiteau notes that many 'smart' projects did not deliver real operational outputs, with "smart money" going to non-core systems (intelligent parking, facial recognition, cosmetic SCADA upgrades) or failed IT developments.

- Intense competition characterized the market: every big water company invested heavily in IT aiming to spin off divisions and list on the stock market, while countless IoT, SCADA, GIS, and IT providers fought price wars—many did not survive. The COVID period and lack of infrastructure stimulus caused significant financing issues and restructuring, though the market is showing signs of recovery.

- Chinese firms stand out for their ability to accumulate experience quickly despite high failure rates. Investment will continue, propelling water technologies globally as Chinese firms get more involved in international projects.

- Smart water technologies (Digital Twins, 3D BIM models, IoT, BI tools) are widely adopted. Competition keeps costs relatively low. Surviving vendors will emerge as local and global players.

- Lhopiteau's French company reinvented both its technology and business model through two decades in the Chinese water market, becoming more resilient and battle-tested for global competition.

- AI use is progressing: algorithms for real-time contaminant detection claim 95% accuracy in pathogen identification; AI-powered acoustic sensors claim 85% leak detection in Beijing's network (non-revenue water losses up to 30% nationally); Beijing piloted swarm robot technology for sludge removal and pipe cleaning with efficiency gains up to 40%.

- China is the world leader in scalable IoT and big data, with projects over one million IoT devices in urban water networks (e.g., Shenzhen). AI for flood and drought management is claimed to reach accuracy levels far superior to the West.

- Three opportunity areas for international companies: 1) the Foreign Investment Encouraged Catalogue (NDRC/MOFCOM policy encouraging foreign expertise and investment in water); 2) the Belt and Road Initiative opening avenues for business with Chinese firms in overseas projects (Southeast Asia, Africa); 3) rural water infrastructure with multilateral agency funding (e.g., World Bank), though Lowest-Priced Technically Acceptable tenders favor local players.

- China lags in interoperability and standardisation (data silos, slow ISO 50001 adoption), though Lhopiteau views this as temporary, citing China's early involvement in designing ISO 55000 (national standard GB/T 33172) and its capacity for fast standardisation demonstrated in power generation.

- The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), currently in drafting, emphasizes AI for 'new quality productive forces' in water with indications of €50+ billion investment for 'water security' amid climate risks. Likely outcomes include AI mandates, potential calls for increased international firm involvement in PPP projects (currently only Suez, Veolia, and Sembcorp remain as foreign water players in China), continued priorities on rural infrastructure and cutting water losses, and water tech exports via Belt and Road.

The article also promotes Aquatech China, the leading water technology trade show in China, running November 5-7 in Shanghai.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Adoption accelerated post-2020 with the 'Digital Water' initiative, with Smart Water solutions deployed in 70 per cent of new wastewater treatment plants for predictive maintenance and leak detection." - Lhopiteau
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: How innovative solutions help Veolia to drive ecological transformation with its stakeholders ---
URL: https://journals.openedition.org/factsreports/7249

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published in Field Actions Science Reports (Special Issue 25, 2023, pp. 48-53), is written by Catherine Ricou, Head of Innovation at Veolia. It explores how Veolia uses innovative solutions to drive ecological transformation with its stakeholders. Ricou became Head of Innovation in 2022, is a graduate of AgroParisTech with over 25 years of experience in environmental management (water, waste, and energy recovery), and now leads innovation for the combined Veolia-Suez scope.

KEY FACTS AND CONTEXT:
- Veolia has set a target to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, invested 165 million euros in 2022, operates 14 R&D centers globally, and holds nearly 5,000 patents.
- In 2022, Veolia published its new statement of purpose: "We develop and implement locally solutions to depollute our vital resources and preserve them from depletion, solutions to decarbonize our ways of living and producing and adapt them to the consequences of climate change."
- In 2022, Veolia's actions helped avoid 14 MtCO2 emissions and saved 320 million m³ of water compared to 2019 through reducing network leakages.
- Veolia weights and rates all new innovation solutions regarding their net contribution to ecological transformation.

MAJOR INNOVATION PILLARS AND EXAMPLES:
1. CIRCULAR MATERIALS: Veolia is circularizing electric vehicle battery production (from mechanical recycling to refining lithium and strategic metals) and developed Plastiloop, the first global integrated platform for circular polymers with 37 plastic recycling plants worldwide. Plastiloop's key innovation is its demand-based approach—starting with the end product and customer requirements rather than "recycling waste and finding uses for it."

2. DEPOLLUTION: Roughly 33% of the world's soil is degraded (per FAO), largely due to chemical fertilizer overuse. Veolia has developed technologies including zero-liquid discharge solutions, reverse osmosis processes, and flue gas treatment, while also working to minimize secondary environmental impacts (energy footprint and supplemental chemicals) of these treatments.

3. GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE: Veolia is shifting from gray to green-and-gray infrastructure. The Urban Flood Park La Marjal in Alicante, Spain (3.6 hectares), a 50-50 joint venture between Aguas de Alicante and Alicante City Council, protects against flooding while reviving biodiversity. It features Mediterranean native vegetation, two purpose-built ponds mimicking Mediterranean wetlands, water retention, a circular water management system with cascade oxygenation and aerators, with shared operation between the City Council and Aguas de Alicante.

4. FROM VOLUME TO VALUE: On May 11, 2023, Veolia renewed a contract to supply water to the Lille metropolitan area for ten years—the first in France to stipulate a 10% reduction in water consumption with financial penalties if unmet. Veolia will install 5,000 sensors/probes, renew nearly 12,000 drinking water connections, use the "leak alert" system via Vig'iléo (an extension of Hubgrade hypervision centers) to detect leaks within 48 hours, provide "consumption coaches" to 1.2 million consumers, and aim to finalize 1,200 water-saving contracts targeting 15% reduction each.

CULTIVATING INNOVATION SPIRIT:
- INSIDE: Veolia (220,000+ employees) launched the Innovation Academy in 2022 to boost innovative mindsets, develop innovation programs across business units, and train all employees.
- OUTSIDE: Veolia develops Open Innovation ecosystems, invests in start-up incubators (e.g., PureControl for optimizing energy consumption in wastewater treatment plants), and partners with scientific and academic institutions.

CONCLUSION: Ricou argues that innovation combines technological and business model innovations, and that any company can adopt the principle of supporting others' ecological transformation through deep investment in people, fostering an innovation mindset, and working outside organizational walls for speed and scale—adopting business models where "your company does well when the planet benefits."
</summary>
