# Cleaned Research Findings: Technological Innovation & Industrialized Commercialization in Chinese Water Supply Enterprises (2016–2026) vs. International Benchmarks

---

## List of Queries and Tool Calls Made

**Round 1 – Chinese water industry context & major utilities:**
- "中国水务 科技创新 产业化 2016 2026 智慧水务 发展现状"
- "北京自来水集团 上海城投水务 深圳水务集团 智慧水务 数字化转型 科技创新"
- "中国城镇供水排水协会 智慧水务 漏损控制 产销差率 报告 2024"

**Round 2 – Chinese water companies, technology providers & international benchmarks:**
- "北控水务 碧水源 科技创新 膜技术 研发投入 专利 智慧水务"
- "首创环保 北京自来水集团 科技 创新 研发投入 智慧水务"
- "粤海水务 洪城环境 中国水务 科技创新 产业化"
- "深圳水务集团 金科环境 津膜科技 南方泵业 威派格 新天科技 智能水表 技术创新"
- "Veolia Suez water utility innovation digital transformation AMI leakage AI comparison China water utilities"
- "international water utility benchmark smart water digital twin non-revenue water leakage Anglian Water PUB Singapore innovation"
- "water utility R&D investment comparison patent portfolio Veolia Suez Beijing Enterprises Water Group"

**Round 3 – Specific companies, technology providers & comparison data:**
- "北京自来水集团 科技创新 智慧供水 数字孪生 漏损 研发"
- "洪城环境 中国水务 金科环境 津膜科技 南方泵业 技术创新 产业化 膜"
- "中国水务企业 研发投入强度 对比 国际 威立雅 苏伊士 水务 专利"
- "威立雅 苏伊士 中国 供水 水务 项目 技术 合作 创新"
- "碧水源 膜 产业化 资源化 再生水 反渗透 国产化"

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

---

### PART 1: MACRO CONTEXT OF CHINA'S WATER UTILITIES INDUSTRY (2016–2026)

**Overall industry status (per ChinaIRN, March 2026)** [1]: China's water utilities industry has entered a "high-quality development stage." Key 2024 statistics: total national water usage was stable at 592.8 billion cubic meters (5928亿立方米); water use per 10,000 yuan GDP and per 10,000 yuan industrial added value dropped 17.7% and 23.6% respectively versus 2020; agricultural irrigation water efficiency coefficient rose to 0.580; **urban public water supply pipeline leakage dropped below 9%**; and rural tap water penetration reached 94% in 2024 (96% target achieved by 2025). Core drivers for 2026-2030 include the "15th Five-Year Plan" policy top-level design (water resource intensive use, ecological protection, urban-rural water integration, smart water management), ecological civilization construction, and dual-carbon goals. Key pain points include: regional imbalances in infrastructure (rural/western areas lagging), uneven digital/smart transformation (SMEs rely on traditional operations), incomplete market-based pricing mechanisms limiting profitability, shortage of professional talent, and **reliance on imported high-end equipment**. Competitive landscape: "state-owned enterprises leading, diversified participation, regional segmentation." Competition is shifting from project contracting to comprehensive competition in operations, technology, service quality, and smart capabilities. Future trends (2026-2030): smart water utilities will achieve industry-wide penetration using big data, IoT, AI, and digital twins; water resource recycling (reclaimed water, rainwater, seawater desalination) and green low-carbon transformation will accelerate; industry focus shifts from infrastructure construction to "construction + operations + quality improvement."

**Smart water market size (per Qianzhan Industry Research Institute, Jan 2022)** [3]: The 2020 smart water services market size in China was approximately **12.48 billion yuan (124.8亿元)**; projected to reach **37 billion yuan (370亿元) by 2026**. China's urban water supply pipeline length reached 920,100 km in 2019 (supply coverage 98.78%), growing to approximately 964,100 km in 2020 (coverage 98.98%). Wastewater discharge: 2019 total 87.3 billion tons (55.5B urban, 10.2B county, 21.6B village); 2020 estimated 92.6 billion tons. Policy evolution: from 2014 through the "14th Five-Year Plan," national support policies evolved from "developing smart water" (发展智能水务) to "developing intelligent water" (发展智慧水务) to "building a smart water conservancy system" (构建智慧水利体系). Key listed companies in the sector: 海峡创新 (300300), **新天科技 (300259)**, 汉威科技 (300007), 三川智慧 (300066), 科陆电子 (002121), 国电南瑞 (600406).

**Dongwu Securities Smart Water Industry Deep Report (Jan 2021)** [5]: The combined market space for smart water platforms + smart water plants (prefabricated) + pipeline network retrofit equipment (including secondary water supply equipment and smart water meters) **exceeds 300 billion RMB (千亿级别/3000亿+)**. Industry concentration is extremely low — leading listed companies hold less than 1% market share. Four key industry drivers: (1) National policy requirements — China's drinking water quality lags the US by 50 years and Japan by 100 years; China's 2017 average urban pipeline leakage rate was **14.71% (2018: 14.62%, with 8.179 billion tons lost)**, significantly higher than developed countries; national policies target leakage under 10% by 2020 and mandate smart water infrastructure; (2) Technology maturation — 5G, NB-IoT, cloud computing, IoT (NB-IoT enables smart meters, DMA zoning, GIS, real-time leakage monitoring); (3) Unified construction and management (统建统管) — provinces including Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hebei, Shandong, Fujian, Guangxi adopting unified secondary water supply models; (4) Rural drinking water upgrades during the 14th Five-Year Plan — estimated one county-level rural upgrade costs ~50 million RMB, implying 100-billion+ RMB market. Market size breakdown: smart water platform market projected to grow from 82.3 billion (2018) to 251.05 billion (2023E); smart water plants (prefabricated): a 3,000-ton/day plant sells for ~20 million RMB, with ~20,000 traditional water plants nationwide, market space estimated at 100+ billion RMB; pipeline network retrofit equipment estimated at 100+ billion RMB. As of H1 2020, there were ~840 smart water enterprises in China (413 manufacturing, 222 IT/software). Major tech entrants: **Huawei won Shenzhen Smart Water Phase I project for 446 million RMB (Dec 2019)**; Tencent Cloud formed strategic partnership with Guangdong Yuehai Water.

**Digital water development status (Prof. Wang Aijie, State Key Laboratory of Urban Water Resource and Environment, HIT — 2023 lecture)** [4]: A 2017-2020 survey of 194 representative water enterprises showed widespread attention and high value recognition for digital water construction. China's digital water construction is transitioning from automation and informatization toward smart/intelligent development. Water supply enterprises focus information systems on customer service (billing, WeChat public accounts, installation management); drainage enterprises focus on operational control (automation, water quality online monitoring, central control systems). Goals include unmanned water plant regulation, scientific pipeline network dispatch, and efficient process control. Half of surveyed enterprises have established independent digital management departments; leading enterprises are characterized by strong leadership attention and deep business department involvement. Government digital water procurement projects are concentrated in southeastern and central China. **China has 95 national-level research projects related to "smart + water."** China's digital water research emphasizes application and practical water issues (water quality monitoring, pollution control), **while Europe and the US focus more on theory and method innovation (big data model/algorithm development)**. Chinese digital water algorithms focus on AI-based watershed pollution tracing and risk prediction. Three urgent needs: (1) improved cognition of digitalization at the leadership level; (2) coordinated, unified construction and industry-recognized digital water standards (avoiding fragmented "each fighting for themselves"); (3) specialized digital water talent (universities lack relevant courses). Additional problems: difficulty integrating technology with business operations; **difficulty measuring digital water benefits (projects rarely generate independent economic returns)**; difficulty forming effective industrial collaboration and core technology development.

**Regulatory/policy infrastructure (CUWA official site)** [12]: The China Urban Water Association (中国城镇供水排水协会/CUWA) is a national, industry-wide, non-profit social organization founded in 1985, supervised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD). Recent key policy documents (2026): 《生态保护"十五五"规划》 (2026-08-12), 《海水淡化产业发展行动方案》 (2026-07-17), and critically **《供水条例》 (Water Supply Regulations, State Council Order No. 831), issued 2026-02-14**. CUWA history highlights: 2024 — won the 2023 National Science and Technology Progress Award First Prize; 2022 — published 《城镇水务系统碳核算与减排路径技术指南》 and 《城镇水务行业年度发展报告（2021）》; 2021 — published **《城镇水务2035年行业发展规划纲要》**; 2020 — established sponge city, water market development, smart water, and youth worker committees; 2018 — completed revision to 《城镇供水管网漏损控制及评定标准》 with Beijing Water Group.

**New Water Supply Regulations impact (Develop Technology keynote at CUWA 2026 Annual Conference, per China Daily)** [13]: At the CUWA 2026 Annual Conference (April 16-18, 2026, Shenzhen; 300+ companies), Ma Yue (马悦), General Manager of Develop Technology's Domestic Water Business Unit, explained that the new 《供水条例》 "impose rigid constraints on water source security, water quality compliance, and water pressure compliance, while linking water pricing to costs—making uncontrolled production-sales gap (产销差) directly lead to revenue loss. Pipe network leakage not only raises the production-sales gap, but also triggers water pressure fluctuations, rising water quality risks, exacerbating water source waste and operational pressure." Industry challenges highlighted: limited effectiveness of traditional leak control and **data silos that hinder refined operations and cost reduction**.

**CUWA 2026 Annual Meeting comprehensive session (April 17, 2026, Shenzhen)** [15]: Thousands of attendees from 31 provinces, Hong Kong, and Macau. Four priority areas for 2026 (opening year of "15th Five-Year Plan"): (a) Strengthen water supply safety under the newly revised Water Supply Regulations; (b) Improve drainage and flood control capacity; (c) Deepen sewage treatment efficiency with pipe network upgrades and reclaimed water utilization; (d) Strengthen industry support through regulations, smart upgrades, and talent development. China Water Association President Zhang Linwei announced **three focus areas**: (1) **Digital transformation** — integrating internet, big data, and AI into water supply/drainage scenarios, building water industry AI databases, promoting energy-saving technologies; (2) **Price mechanism reform** — supporting water price hearing system reforms and sewage treatment fee mechanism transitions; (3) **Market integration** — increasing industry concentration and cultivating leading water enterprises under the national unified market policy. Shenzhen's achievements reported: world-leading pipe network leakage rates, water consumption per 10,000 yuan GDP at only 1/7 of the national average, first open-source HarmonyOS secondary water supply pump house and water purification plant, and 90-day water supply reserves via the Xijiang River diversion. Gong Limin (深圳环境水务集团董事长) reported: **99%+ digital coverage, 30% improved O&M efficiency through digital twin systems, 97% customer satisfaction, pipe network leakage rates below 5%**. Professor Ren Nanqi presented on digital twin applications including a watershed pollution digital twin platform built after the 2005 Songhua River nitrobenzene pollution incident. Professor Peng Yongzhen presented AOA technology (outperforms AAO in nitrogen/phosphorus removal, sludge reduction, energy savings; total nitrogen below 8.0 mg/L even at 13°C). Hong Kong Water Supplies Department Director Wong Yan-nok shared Hong Kong's 60+ year seawater toilet flushing system experience.

**Carbon neutrality / industry value analysis (21st Century Business Herald / Qianji Investment Bank, March 2021)** [29]: Industry characteristics: strong regional monopoly, geographic limitations, long-term stable development, low marketization and profitability, and **a technology gap versus international peers**. Top 10 water companies hold only 9% market concentration in urban water supply. Supply market: 80% state-owned, 10% private, 10% foreign; sewage treatment: 48% state, 30% foreign, 22% private. Business models: primarily franchise (特许经营) models — competitive (委托运营, BOT, TOT, overall franchise) and exclusive types. Sewage treatment uses "government franchise, government procurement, enterprise operation" with prices re-evaluated every 3 years. Technology highlights: NB-IoT smart water meters (10-year battery life, 50-100x more connections, 20dB+ better coverage than GPRS). 2035 rural sewage treatment rate projected at 70%, creating a 200 billion RMB market. Key Chinese companies listed: 重庆水务[601158.SH], 首创股份[600008.SH], 兴蓉环境[000598.SZ], 中山公用[000685.SZ], 创业环保[600874.SH], 粤海投资[0270.HK], **北控水务集团[0371.HK], 中国水务[0855.HK]**. International players: 威立雅 (Veolia), 苏伊士 (Suez), Thames Water, American Water[AWK.N], Severn Trent[SVT.L], California Water[CWT.N].

**Water pricing context (Huafu Securities report on United Water, Dec 2024)** [14]: Water utilities operate under 25-30 year concession models with geographic and franchise barriers. Between March 2013 and March 2024, residential water prices in 36 key Chinese cities rose from 1.91 to 2.35 yuan/ton (CAGR ~1.90%). **Compared to international standards, Chinese water prices remain very low (Beijing's water costs are less than 1/10 of Berlin or Copenhagen; Sydney, Singapore, London, and Paris charge 6-7 times Beijing's rates)**. #### 6.2 Leakage/NRW performance
- China: urban leakage 14.71% (2017), 14.62% (2018), 12.9%/12.5% (2022), **below 9% nationally (2024)**; provincial range 10.1% (Zhejiang) to 16.7% (Liaoning) in 2022; policy target ≤9% by 2025 [5][1][14]. Best-in-class Chinese: Shenzhen below 5% [15]; Shantou Yuehai 6.58% [11]; 首创环保 12.20% (9 consecutive years of decline) [21].
- International: Japan and US below 8% [14]; one-fifth of UK water lost through leakage annually [48]; Singapore 4.1 reported leaks per 100km (2022) [40]; Veolia achieved 15% leakage reduction in Prague [36]; Suez claims leak detection time reduced by 75%, water losses reduced by at least 30% [37]; Anglian Water industry-leading low leakage, half as many leaks as any other UK company per km [41].

#### 6.3 R&D investment levels
- Chinese companies: 首创环保 R&D investment RMB 212 million in 2025 (on 18.886 billion yuan revenue — roughly 1.1% intensity) [21][22]; OriginWater R&D 343 million yuan = 4.01% of main business revenue (2024) [72]; 南方泵业 R&D 265 million yuan = 4.88% of revenue (2023) [58]; BEWG holds 772 patents + 420 software copyrights (2022) [17]; 首创环保 1,185 cumulative authorized patents (2025) [23]; OriginWater full-chain membrane IP + 60+ patents in seawater desalination [21]. 首创环保 "14th FYP" targets: R&D intensity of 2%, 120 invention patents [25].
- International: Veolia Water Technologies has **350+ patented technologies** [60][69]; Suez Digital Solutions unit has **600+ data and AI experts** [37]; Veolia Hubgrade operates 10,000+ connected sites with 60 monitoring centers and 500 experts/data scientists [36]. No direct international R&D-spend-as-% of revenue figures captured, but the structural gap is in dedicated digital/AI expert headcount and global SaaS deployment scale.

#### 6.4 Technology commercialization pathways
- Chinese models: (1) franchise/PPP/BOT/ROT with minimum water volume guarantees (OriginWater) [18]; (2) light-asset transformation — BEWG's Beishui Future Technology and Beishui Cloud Services; 首创环保 light-asset orders 72.80% of new contracts [24][20]; (3) technology product launch events (BEWG BEAOA & Speed Granule "first step of technology commercialization" toward "replicable, large-scale standardized products") [17]; (4) prefabricated/assembled products (BEWG Speed Granule — China's first prefabricated municipal aerobic granular sludge product; Weipage smart water plants; Jinke New Water Island with 3-month construction, 1/6 footprint) [17][5][74]; (5) PIPP/Blue Eco-Park models selling reclaimed water to industrial B-end clients (Jinke) [74]; (6) data asset monetization — first water data asset transactions/certificates (南京, 上海城投水务, 广州水投) [32].
- International models: (1) Veolia's "technology premium" model — minority equity in investment companies, majority in operating companies, separating services into related-party contracts for fee collection at each operational stage (Qingdao case: 40% investment stake / 78% operating stake) [66]; (2) Suez's JV + concession model (Macao 25+20 year concession) [63]; (3) SaaS-based digital solution offerings (Veolia Hubgrade all solutions in SaaS mode; Suez On'connect/Aquadvanced/AssetAdvanced as products) [39][37]; (4) Metering-as-a-Service (Badger Meter netAMP subscription model) [45]; (5) Ofwat Innovation Fund competitive grants (Severn Trent £2M Water Breakthrough Challenge; £1.7 billion PR24 for smart meters) [47][46].

#### 6.5 Revenue models
- Chinese: low water prices (Beijing <1/10 of Berlin/Copenhagen; 36 key cities 1.91→2.35 yuan/ton 2013-2024); pricing formula reform (permitted costs + reasonable returns); tiered pricing 1:1.5:3; sewage treatment "government franchise, government procurement, enterprise operation" with 3-year price re-evaluations [14][29]. Reclaimed water utilization rate only 25.8% vs developed countries' 60-70% [74].
- International: French delegated management (concession and affermage/lease contracts); private companies controlled 96% of French market (Veolia 36.7%, Suez 18.8%, SAUR 40%) [69]; Veolia's average dividend yield 5.43% over 10 years [69]; UK regulatory price reviews (Ofwat PR24) with innovation funding [46]; rising block tariffs (Affinity Water WaterSave trial) [46].

#### 6.6 Patent portfolios
- Chinese: BEWG 772 patents + 420 software copyrights (2022) [17]; 首创环保 1,185 cumulative authorized patents (163 invention) [21][23]; OriginWater full-chain membrane IP, 60+ seawater desalination patents, Chinese Patent Excellence Award [21]; 津膜科技 2 National Technology Invention Second Prizes + National Science and Technology Progress First Prize (2024) [55]; 南方泵业 added 10 invention + 60 utility + 5 design patents in 2023 [58].
- International: Veolia Water Technologies 350+ patents [60]; no aggregate portfolio data captured for Suez/Anglian/PUB in gathered sources.

#### 6.7 Deployment scale of smart water systems
- China: ~840 smart water enterprises (2020) [5]; smart water market 12.48 billion yuan (2020) → 37 billion yuan (2026E) [3]; Huawei Shenzhen Smart Water Phase I 446 million RMB [5]; Shenzhen 99%+ digital coverage, 100% online monitoring via smart meters (Shenshan) [9][15]; Shantou Yuehai 632 monitoring meters, 66% remote rate, 71% of water volume monitored [11]; Chengtou Water 60+ robot applications planned by 2026 [7]; 95 national-level "smart + water" research projects [4].
- International: Veolia 10,000+ connected sites, 640+ connected sites for digital solutions, 4,400 active users, 30+ countries [36][39]; Suez 7 million smart meters deployed worldwide, 1,500+ smart water customers, 45,000 connected waste objects [37]; UK plan ~10 million smart meters by 2030 (48% coverage), 73% by 2040 [46]; Anglian 500,000+ meters fitted, 1.1M target by 2025, 1.2M more 2025-2030 [41]; Severn Trent ~600,000 meters [49]; US ~40% AMI conversion [45]; PUB Smart Water Grid with hundreds of monitoring stations [40].

#### 6.8 Regulatory incentives
- China: policy evolution from "smart water" to "smart water conservancy system" (2014-14th FYP) [3]; leakage targets (<10% by 2020, <9% by 2025) [5][14]; 15th FYP opening with Water Supply Regulations (2026) imposing rigid constraints and price-cost linkage [13]; 800亿超长期特别国债 for underground pipe networks [32]; water resource fee-to-tax nationwide Dec 2024 [32]; CUWA annual science & technology awards (e.g., Chengtou 2024 Second Prize) [8]; 3+1 rural water supply model [2]; digital China "2522" framework [4]; 100 green low-carbon benchmark sewage plants by 2025 [32]; reclaimed water 3-year action plan in 50 cities [21].
- International: Ofwat PR24 £1.7 billion for ~10 million smart meters; Water Breakthrough Challenge innovation grants [47][46]; EU Drinking Water Directive PFAS limits now binding (2026) [35]; UK Environment Agency 2050 water deficit projections (demand would exceed supply by 5 billion litres/day by 2050 without intervention) driving smart meter rollout [46].

#### 6.9 Innovation ecosystem maturity
- China: identified weaknesses — leadership cognition of digitalization; lack of unified digital water standards ("each fighting for themselves"); shortage of specialized digital water talent (universities lack courses); difficulty integrating technology with business; **difficulty measuring digital water benefits (projects rarely generate independent economic returns)**; difficulty forming effective industrial collaboration and core technology development [4]. Reliance on imported high-end equipment [1]. Technology gap versus international peers [29]. Core technology gaps in seawater desalination and industrial water (GWI's 2020 top-10 water technology breakthroughs list featured no Chinese companies) [61]. Standards differences and unfamiliarity with European/American standards hinder overseas expansion [61].
- International: mature innovation ecosystems — Veolia Hubgrade combining innovation and digital know-how across three businesses [36]; Suez Digital Solutions unit with 600+ AI experts [37]; Ofwat innovation fund ecosystem with multi-utility collaboration (Severn Trent with 4 other utilities + Microsoft, BT, Rockwell) [47]; Anglian Water Innovation Hub [43]; PUB's Smart Water Grid with Bentley machine learning [40]; satellite leak detection start-up ecosystem (Origin Tech, 12 UK water companies) [48].

#### 6.10 Similarities
- Both Chinese and international utilities are deploying digital twins, AI leak detection, smart metering (NB-IoT/WIZE/LoRa), and intelligent plant operations.
- Both are pursuing asset-light transformation and service-based revenue (Veolia operation-led model; Chinese light-asset platforms) [20][65][66].
- Both face aging infrastructure and leakage as top priorities.
- Both are integrating AI large models/agents into operations (Veolia Hubgrade AI; BEWG "Enki" vertical large model; DeepSeek deployments at Jinke/Weipage) [19][32][36].
- Both emphasize water resource recovery and membrane technology (OriginWater MBR-DF; Suez/Veolia membrane portfolios).
- Both are entering each other's domains: Chinese companies expanding overseas (United Water Dhaka; OriginWater Serbia/Russia/Malaysia; BEWG "Belt and Road"), while Veolia/Suez remain significant in China's market.

#### 6.11 Key differences / gaps summary
1. **Scale of international digital platforms**: Veolia's 10,000+ connected sites and Suez's 7 million smart meters dwarf individual Chinese utility deployments (though China's national smart water market is growing rapidly).
2. **Commercialization of digital products**: International firms monetize digital solutions as SaaS products (Hubgrade, Aquadvanced, AssetAdvanced, Metering-as-a-Service) with documented ROI (leak detection time -75%, capex -30%, energy -20%); Chinese digital water projects "rarely generate independent economic returns" [4] and are often bundled into larger construction/EPC projects.
3. **Innovation funding mechanisms**: UK Ofwat innovation funds and price reviews provide dedicated, competitive R&D funding tied to regulatory performance; China relies more on national policy mandates and SOE internal budgets.
4. **R&D focus**: China emphasizes application and practical water issues; Europe/US focus on theory, method innovation, and big data model/algorithm development [4].
5. **Market concentration & pricing**: Chinese market fragmented (top 10 = 9% concentration), water prices far below international levels, limiting funds available for innovation investment; French market historically 96% controlled by three private companies with mature delegated management.
6. **Standardization**: China lacks unified digital water standards; Europe/US have established regulatory frameworks (Ofwat, EU Drinking Water Directive) driving technology adoption.
7. **Leakage performance spread**: Best-in-class Chinese utilities (Shenzhen <5%, Shantou Yuehai 6.58%) approach international benchmarks, but national average (9% in 2024) still exceeds Japan/US (<8%) and best international performers.
8. **Patent/talent depth**: International firms maintain large dedicated digital/AI expert teams (Suez 600+; Veolia 500 experts/data scientists); Chinese firms rely more on university partnerships and national labs, with recognized talent shortages.

### PART 7: RECOMMENDED TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTIONS (技术攻关方向) — SUPPORTING EVIDENCE BASE

The research question asks for 3-5 key technology development directions for Chinese water utilities to achieve successful industrialized commercialization, tied to identified gaps and mapping to successful international commercialization models. The following evidence directly supports such recommendations:

**Direction A: AI-driven leakage control and DMA optimization** — Supported by: China's remaining leakage gap (national 9% vs. best-in-class 6.58%/below 5% [15][11], international <8% [14]); Shantou Yuehai's successful technology-enabled DMA program (365 zones, 632 meters, 71% volume monitored, 13.1%→6.58%) [11]; international models: Suez Aquadvanced (leak detection time -75%, losses -30%) [37], Thames Water/Origin Tech satellite AI (30-metre radius, 800+ leaks in trial) [48], PUB ALF machine learning digital twin [40], Veolia Waterloss Management [39], Anglian smart meters finding 100,000+ leaks [41].

**Direction B: Digital twin platforms for water networks** — Supported by: Shenzhen's digital twin adaptive dispatch (China's first "no human intervention" model; energy -5%, labor -35.6%) [9]; Chengtou Water digital twin award-winning unmanned dispatch [8]; PUB's live digital twin with ALF [40]; Veolia Hubgrade digital twin (100+ installations, 30-100% capacity/energy/chemical gains) [39][38]; Anglian/Qatium field-technician digital twins [43]; Suez Aquadvanced/AssetAdvanced [37].

**Direction C: Advanced membrane water treatment industrialization** — Supported by: China's 25.8% reclaimed water reuse vs. 60-70% international [74]; OriginWater's full-chain membrane self-reliance, MBR 70% domestic share, V-MBR energy/cost reductions, Membrane Cloud digital service system [18][72][73]; 津膜科技's CMF/SMF/MBR with National Science and Technology Progress First Prize [55]; Jinke's productization (New Water Island, 3-month construction, 1/6 footprint; PIPP model) and GWI Global Water Award [74]; membrane market 500 billion yuan projected by 2025 [21]; policy push for reclaimed water in 50 cities [21].

**Direction D: Intelligent plant unmanned operations** — Supported by: Chengtou Water "Sea-Land-Air" robot inspection (50% manual hours reduction, 60% emergency response improvement) and Nanshi smart factory (8 million yuan annual savings) [7]; BEWG "Enki" vertical large model for adaptive sewage plant control [19]; Shenzhen Bao'an adaptive dispatch [9]; international: Veolia Hubgrade Performance Plant digital twin [39]; Severn Trent AI waste catchment autonomy with £2M Ofwat funding [47]; the industry direction toward "unmanned/minimal-staffed" plants (most prefecture-level water groups expected to launch smart plant upgrades by end-2026) [53].

**Direction E: Smart metering data monetization** — Supported by: first Chinese water data asset transactions/certificates (南京, 上海城投水务, 广州水投) [32]; BEWG "Yunlian Wang" transforming water assets into data assets [19]; international: Suez 7 million smart meters with On'connect (16% customer savings) [37]; UK ~10 million smart meter plan with £1.7 billion Ofwat funding [46]; Badger Meter Metering-as-a-Service netAMP subscription model and 27 billion gallons savings [45]; Anglian £15 million annual customer savings from smart meters [41].

**Direction F: Water resource recovery** — Supported by: China's low reclaimed water utilization (25.8% vs 60-70% developed countries) [74]; OriginWater MBR-DF converting sewage to Class II/III surface water, seawater desalination breakthroughs, salt lake lithium [18][21][73]; Jinke PIPP/Blue Eco-Park industrial water sales [74]; policy timeline accelerating wastewater resource utilization (2021-2024) [21]; international: Veolia circular economy TS2A sorting with 95%+ recovery [69]; Suez industrial park circular economy services [60].

args.research_topic:
Research the state of technological innovation and its industrialized commercialization in Chinese water supply and water production enterprises (自来水生产及销售企业/Chinese water utilities) over the period 2016-2026, and conduct a comparative analysis against international (non-Chinese) water utility benchmarks such as Veolia, SUEZ, Xylem, Grundfos, PUB Singapore, Anglian Water, and Badger Meter in terms of technological innovation and commercialization capabilities. Identify specific gaps, differences, and similarities. Use Chinese-language sources as priority (including 中国城镇供水排水协会 publications, 水务企业年报 (corporate annual reports), 招投标信息 (bidding information), 证券研究报告 (securities research reports), 新华网/人民网 industry reports, 北极星水处理网, E20环境平台, and Chinese company official websites).

Key Chinese water utilities and technology companies to cover: 北京自来水集团 (Beijing Waterworks Group), 上海城投水务 (Shanghai Chengtou Water Group), 深圳水务集团 (Shenzhen Water Group), 广州市自来水公司, 首创环保/首创股份 (Capital Eco-Environment Protection Group), 北控水务 (Beijing Enterprises Water Group / BEWG), 碧水源 (OriginWater), 中国水务 (China Water Affairs Group), 粤海水务 (Guangdong Yuehai Water Group), 洪城环境, 金科环境 (Golder Environment), 津膜科技 (Tianjin Motimo), 南方泵业 (Nanfang Pump), 威派格 (WePuke), 新天科技 (Suntront).

Innovation areas to examine in the Chinese context: 智能水表/智慧水务 (smart metering and AMI), AI漏损检测/DMA分区计量 (AI leak detection and DMA pressure management), 数字孪生 (digital twins for water networks), 产销差率/漏损控制 (non-revenue water reduction), 膜技术(超滤/反渗透) (membrane technology for water treatment), 智慧水厂 (intelligent water plant operations), 高品质饮用水/深度处理 (advanced water treatment for high-quality drinking water), and 资源回收 (resource recovery).

For the comparison, examine specific dimensions: (1) R&D investment levels as percentage of revenue for Chinese water utilities versus international peers, (2) technology commercialization pathways and revenue models (e.g., whether Chinese utilities license/export technology, form technology spin-offs, or monetize data), (3) patent portfolios and intellectual property, (4) deployment scale of smart water systems (e.g., number of smart meters, DMA coverage, leakage rate achievements in cities like 深圳/上海/北京), (5) regulatory incentives (e.g., 十四五规划 water policy, 国家发改委 and 住建部 regulations on 漏损率 targets, water tariff reform), (6) innovation ecosystem maturity (university-industry collaboration, 专精特新小巨人 water technology firms), and (7) key economic/financial metrics of Chinese water utilities (e.g., 北控水务 and 首创环保 revenue, smart water contract values from 威派格/金科环境 annual reports).

Then, based on the comparison findings, propose 3-5 key technology development directions (技术攻关方向) that Chinese water utilities should prioritize to achieve successful industrialized commercialization of technological innovations. For each recommended direction, provide: (a) the specific technology direction with name in Chinese and English, (b) rationale tied to identified gaps versus international leaders, (c) how it maps to successful international commercialization models (e.g., metering-as-a-service like Badger Meter, digital twin SaaS like Bentley/Autodesk, energy recovery hardware like Energy Recovery Inc., NEWater-style water reuse industrialization), and (d) suggested implementation pathways for Chinese water enterprises. Produce a structured report with the Chinese water utility landscape, the comparative gap analysis, and the 3-5 strategic recommendations.

# Research Report: Top Commercialized Water Technology Innovations (2016–2026) — International Enterprises

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### A. GLOBAL WATER INDUSTRY LEADERS & MARKET CONTEXT (for ranking context)

**GWI Top Water Businesses Ranking (Global Water Intelligence, 2025 list based on 2024 water revenues):**
- **#1 Veolia** — largest global water business by revenue; as a division of Veolia Environnement it generated approximately **€12.5 billion in 2024**, employed nearly **96,000 people** in water-supply and wastewater operations, provided clean water to nearly **95 million people** and wastewater services to about **68 million**.
- **#2 Ecolab** — continued momentum into 2025 including Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.50 (12% YoY increase), reflecting strength in commercial and industrial water treatment services.
- **#3 Xylem** — global water technology revenues of about **$8.6 billion in 2024**, supporting 23,000 employees across 150+ countries; May 2023 acquisition of Evoqua Water Technologies solidified its position as the world's largest pure-play water-technology business.
- **#4 Core & Main** — leading US-based distributor of water, sewer, and stormwater products.
- **#5 Ferguson** — major wholesale supplier of plumbing and HVAC products.
- Solenis rose 6 places, becoming a serious rival to Ecolab through aggressive M&A.
- AECOM, Jacobs, and WSP were the fastest-growing large companies in water last year.
- The Chinese market declined due to the collapse in domestic construction.
- Notable industry forces: smart water technologies, PFAS treatment, decarbonization projects, circular-economy initiatives. [1][4]

**Xylem competitive profile (2024):** Approximately **$8.6 billion 2024 revenue**, ~23,000 employees, 150+ countries; dates to 2011 ITT spin-off; closed **$7.5 billion Evoqua acquisition in 2023**. Competes in water infrastructure, treatment, and smart monitoring. Key competitors: Veolia (2024 revenue ~€44.7 billion; strengthened by 2022 Suez merger), Pentair, Grundfos (pumps/energy-efficient applications), Badger Meter (smart metering; 2024 revenue ~US$827 million), Sulzer, Franklin Electric, Watts Water. Core brands: Flygt, Goulds Water Technology, Sensus, YSI. Evoqua deal broadened treatment coverage. Industry drivers: aging infrastructure (ASCE gave US drinking water infrastructure a D grade in 2025), PFAS compliance (US EPA set first national drinking water limits April 2024), water scarcity, digital leak detection demand, shift to recurring software/service revenue. [2]

**Top 20 Global Industrial Water Service Companies (Spherical Insights, 2026):** Market projected to grow from USD 373.9 billion (2025) to USD 735.5 billion (2035), CAGR 7%. Companies: 1. Veolia Water Technologies, 2. SUEZ Water Technologies & Solutions, 3. Xylem Inc., 4. Ecolab Inc., 5. Kurita Water Industries, 6. Pentair plc, 7. Aquatech International, 8. DuPont Water Solutions, 9. Evoqua Water Technologies, 10. H2O Innovation Inc., 11. Culligan, 12. Danaher Corporation, 13. Dow Water & Process Solutions, 14. 3M Purification, 15. BWT AG, 16. Pall Corporation, 17. GE Water & Process Technologies, 18. Lenntech, 19. Ovivo, 20. Calgon Carbon. Key revenues: Veolia Environnement ~€44.4 billion (2025, 50+ countries, Hubgrade platform); SUEZ Water Technologies ~USD 3.8–4.0 billion (water tech segment); Xylem ~USD 8.5–8.6 billion; Ecolab ~USD 15–16 billion (Nalco Water division); Kurita ~USD 2.0 billion. [3]

**Wastewater Treatment Services Company Evaluation (ResearchAndMarkets, 2025):** Evaluated 62+ companies; top 8 quadrant leaders include Veolia, SUEZ, Xylem Inc., Evoqua Water Technologies, Thermax Limited, Ecolab, WOG Technologies. Technology analysis covers advanced oxidation processes, reverse osmosis, nutrient recovery, electrocoagulation. [5]

---

### B. RANKED INNOVATION CATEGORIES WITH EVIDENCE

#### 1. Smart Water Metering / Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI)

**Market size (multiple sources):**
- Global AMI water meter market valued at **USD 1.6 billion in 2024**, projected to reach **USD 22.3 billion by 2034**, **CAGR 30%** (2025–2034). U.S. EPA reports utilities with AMI can reduce non-revenue water losses by up to 50%; water metering and pricing programs can reduce consumption by 20% or more. Key players: Arad Group, Badger Meter, Diehl, Honeywell, Itron, Kamstrup, Landis+Gyr, Ningbo Water Meter, Sensus, Siemens, Sontex, ZENNER. Itron+Microsoft (May 2021) pilot handled 2.8 billion readings daily in under three hours (10 million meters). [6]
- Smart Water Meter Market: **USD 3.7 billion (2024) → USD 27.5 billion (2034)**, CAGR 22.2%. North America dominates at 46.3% (USD 1.7 Bn). AMI leads at 58.9% share. Water utilities lead adoption at 67.2%. RF communication dominates at 49.3%. Retrofit/replacement deployments lead at 67.9%. Residential leads at 59.5%. [7]
- Bluefield Research (June 6, 2025): smart water metering is a **US$6.8 billion global market**; metering systems account for over 20% of utilities' digital spend in 2024. Top 20 vendors hold 76% of global hardware/software market, led by **Sensus (Xylem), Badger Meter, Neptune Technology Group**. New business models: network-as-a-service (NaaS), metering-as-a-service (MaaS). Spain's €3 billion PERTE initiative and UK AMP8 mandate (10 million smart meters by 2030) driving rollouts. BABA waiver for AMI meters through 2027. [8][20]
- Smart Water Metering Market (Precedence Research): USD 5.22 billion (2025) → USD 15.42 billion (2035), CAGR 11.65%. Asia Pacific largest; North America fastest-growing. SUEZ+Vodafone (April 2024) NB-IoT remote meter reading partnership targeting 2M+ meters by 2030; cuts water consumption up to 15% by detecting leaks. [9]
- Smart Water Metering (InsightAce): USD 5.09 billion (2025) → USD 14.29 billion (2035), CAGR 11.0%. [10]
- Smart Water Meters (MarketsandMarkets): USD 4.61 billion (2024) → USD 9.04 billion (2030), CAGR 11.9%. Top companies: Badger Meter, Sensus (Xylem), Diehl, Landis+Gyr, Itron (200+ million devices deployed). [56]

**Badger Meter, Inc. (NYSE: BMI) — financial evidence of commercial success:**
- **Full Year 2024:** Net sales **$826.6 million** (up 18% from $703.6M in 2023); operating earnings $157.9M; operating margin record **19.1%** (up 230 bps); net earnings $124.9M; diluted EPS $4.23 (up 35%); record cash flow from operations $155.0M. Utility water sales increased 14% in Q4, driven by cellular AMI offerings (ORION Cellular endpoints, BEACON SaaS, mechanical and ultrasonic metering). Announced acquisition of SmartCover® Systems (sewer/lift-station monitoring, ~50% US market share in that niche). [27][10]
- **Q2 2025:** Record quarterly net sales $238.1M (vs $216.7M Q2 2024); operating earnings $44.9M; diluted EPS $1.17; gross margin 41.1% (up 170 bps); utility water sales +11% YoY including SmartCover. Six-month 2025 net sales $460.3M; net earnings $73.0M; EPS $2.47. CEO Kenneth C. Bockhorst cited strong demand for cellular AMI and BlueEdge portfolio. [26]
- **Q3 2025:** Net sales $235.7M; operating earnings $46.1M (margin 19.6%); gross margin 40.7%; EPS $1.19 (up 10%). Utility water sales +14% (8% excluding SmartCover). Nine-month 2025 net sales $696.0M; net earnings $108.1M. Management raised normalized gross margin range to 39–42%. [28]
- **Full Year 2025:** Record net sales **$916.7 million**; operating earnings $183.4M; net earnings $141.6M; diluted EPS **$4.79**; cash flow from operations $183.7M. Acquired SmartCover (January 30, 2025) for **$184.0 million**. Selected by **Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (PRASA)** for one of the world's largest AMI deployments covering **1.6 million service connections** using E-Series Ultrasonic meters, ORION Cellular endpoints, and BEACON SaaS. [29]
- Investment analysis (Daniel's Deep Dive, Jan 2026): ~40% of US water meters use AMI; ~85% of demand tied to replacement cycles; US loses ~19.5% of treated drinking water (~$6.4 billion annually); EPA estimates $625 billion drinking water investment needed by 2041 plus ~$600B wastewater. Badger generates ~90% of revenue in US; recurring revenue ~7% of total growing at 28%; 10-year revenue CAGR ~9%, earnings CAGR ~17%. [30]

**Xylem/Sensus — smart metering:**
- Xylem acquired Sensus (2016) for **approximately $1.7 billion in cash**. Sensus had 80+ million metering devices installed globally; FlexNet® communications network technology; **$837 million adjusted revenue and $159 million adjusted EBITDA in FY2016** (10.7x EBITDA purchase price). Xylem expected at least $50 million in annual cost synergies. AMI segment growing at nearly twice the rate of total metering space. ~70% of Sensus' 2016 revenues were US-generated. [58]
- **2025:** Xylem announced sale of international water/heat metering business (outside North America) to AURELIUS — generated approximately **$250 million in revenues in 2024**. Xylem retains North American smart metering under Sensus name. [59]

**SUEZ smart metering deployments:**
- SUEZ claims: **7 million smart water meters deployed worldwide**; >45,000 connected objects for smart waste; >1,500 customers using smart water systems; 600+ data and AI experts. IoT On'connect range saves up to 16% through reduced consumption/leak detection; saves households up to €200/year. [51]
- **Le Mans Métropole (France):** Since 2018, **120,000 smart water meters** installed (Diehl meters, Wize IoT network, ON'connect, AQUADVANCED® Water Networks). Results: night-time flow reduced by **30 m³/hour** (equivalent to 250,000 m³ saved/year and **€125,000 saved**); drastic reduction in rebate requests; dedicated leak detection unit created. ON'connect processes over 600 million data messages daily. [52]
- Aquadvanced benefits: leak detection time reduced by **75%**; water losses reduced by at least **30%**; energy costs reduced up to **20%**; water purchasing/selling costs reduced up to 10%; 5–10% electricity bill reduction; ROI in under 1 year. [51]

**Dallas Water Utilities / Xylem case study:** DWU (2.4 million customers, 5,000 miles of water mains) saved an average of **7.2 million gallons of water per day** using Xylem's inline acoustic technologies (tethered Sahara® and free-swimming SmartBall®). Located and repaired over **285 leaks** on large-diameter mains; almost **50% reduction in total water main leaks** (from 40 to less than 21 leaks per 100 miles) since 2008. Recovered water value becomes recurring revenue. [86]

**Xylem Revenue Locator (Orange County, CA utility):** Identified ~5% of retail water not registered/unbilled (~2% of top-line revenue); flagged over 1,800 issues; identified over **1 billion gallons of apparent water loss** = historical revenue loss of **over $4 million** if no action taken. Only 6–10% of meters actually required replacement. [87]

**Hot Springs, Arkansas (Sensus/Xylem):** Deployed AMI since 2011 (Sensus iPERL meters, FlexNet); identified and fixed a leak of nearly **4 million gallons per day**; NRW dropped from **44% to 24%** (goal 20%, ultimately 10–12%); virtual DMAs via Xylem Vue found a fire hydrant losing 2,000 gallons/hour. [88]

---

#### 2. Desalination (RO) & Energy Recovery Devices

**Desalination market size:**
- USD 21.72 billion (2024) → USD 51.51 billion (2032), CAGR 11.4% (Credence). Middle East & Africa ~45% share; APAC ~25% fastest-growing; RO dominant technology. Key players: Xylem, Acciona Agua, Hitachi Zosen, Aquatech, Pentair, Hyflux, Veolia, SUEZ, Doosan Enerbility, IDE Technologies, Abengoa, DuPont, Toray, Hydranautics, LG Chem. [17]
- Water Desalination Equipment: US$13.0 Bn (2024) → US$32.3 Bn (2035), CAGR 8.6% (Transparency). RO ~49% of revenues. Key projects: UAE Jebel Ali (2.1 million m³/day), Saudi SWCC (7.5+ million m³/day), Sorek Israel (624,000 m³/day largest RO), Carlsbad (50 MGD). Aquatech awarded Corpus Christi Inner Harbor (30 MGD, first large-scale seawater RO in Texas). Veolia/SIDEM secured US$280 Mn Mirfa 2 RO contract (550,000 m³/day, Abu Dhabi, reducing energy use up to 80%). [18]
- Water Desalination Market: $19.98B (2024) → $51.19B (2035), CAGR 8.93% (MRFR). Energy recovery devices improve efficiency by up to 90%. Key players: Veolia, Suez, Acciona, IDE Technologies, Doosan, Hyflux, Toray, Aqualia. [19]
- Water Desalination: USD 20.62B (2024) → USD 44.03B (2033), CAGR 12.8% (CMI). [20]

**Energy Recovery Device for RO market:**
- Global ERD market reached **USD 2.1 billion in 2024**, projected to **USD 5.2 billion by 2033**, CAGR 10.2%. Pressure exchangers dominate, recovering up to **98% of energy** from brine stream. APAC leads (~USD 700M 2024, 12.3% CAGR); North America + Europe ~USD 850M; MEA ~USD 400M. ### PART 1: MACRO CONTEXT OF CHINA'S WATER UTILITIES INDUSTRY (2016–2026)

**Overall industry status (per ChinaIRN, March 2026)** [1]: China's water utilities industry has entered a "high-quality development stage." Key 2024 statistics: total national water usage was stable at 592.8 billion cubic meters (5928亿立方米); water use per 10,000 yuan GDP and per 10,000 yuan industrial added value dropped 17.7% and 23.6% respectively versus 2020; agricultural irrigation water efficiency coefficient rose to 0.580; **urban public water supply pipeline leakage dropped below 9%**; and rural tap water penetration reached 94% in 2024 (96% target achieved by 2025). Core drivers for 2026-2030 include the "15th Five-Year Plan" policy top-level design (water resource intensive use, ecological protection, urban-rural water integration, smart water management), ecological civilization construction, and dual-carbon goals. Key pain points include: regional imbalances in infrastructure (rural/western areas lagging), uneven digital/smart transformation (SMEs rely on traditional operations), incomplete market-based pricing mechanisms limiting profitability, shortage of professional talent, and **reliance on imported high-end equipment**. Competitive landscape: "state-owned enterprises leading, diversified participation, regional segmentation." Competition is shifting from project contracting to comprehensive competition in operations, technology, service quality, and smart capabilities. Future trends (2026-2030): smart water utilities will achieve industry-wide penetration using big data, IoT, AI, and digital twins; water resource recycling (reclaimed water, rainwater, seawater desalination) and green low-carbon transformation will accelerate; industry focus shifts from infrastructure construction to "construction + operations + quality improvement."

**Smart water market size (per Qianzhan Industry Research Institute, Jan 2022)** [3]: The 2020 smart water services market size in China was approximately **12.48 billion yuan (124.8亿元)**; projected to reach **37 billion yuan (370亿元) by 2026**. China's urban water supply pipeline length reached 920,100 km in 2019 (supply coverage 98.78%), growing to approximately 964,100 km in 2020 (coverage 98.98%). Wastewater discharge: 2019 total 87.3 billion tons (55.5B urban, 10.2B county, 21.6B village); 2020 estimated 92.6 billion tons. Policy evolution: from 2014 through the "14th Five-Year Plan," national support policies evolved from "developing smart water" (发展智能水务) to "developing intelligent water" (发展智慧水务) to "building a smart water conservancy system" (构建智慧水利体系). Key listed companies in the sector: 海峡创新 (300300), **新天科技 (300259)**, 汉威科技 (300007), 三川智慧 (300066), 科陆电子 (002121), 国电南瑞 (600406).

**Dongwu Securities Smart Water Industry Deep Report (Jan 2021)** [5]: The combined market space for smart water platforms + smart water plants (prefabricated) + pipeline network retrofit equipment (including secondary water supply equipment and smart water meters) **exceeds 300 billion RMB (千亿级别/3000亿+)**. Industry concentration is extremely low — leading listed companies hold less than 1% market share. Four key industry drivers: (1) National policy requirements — China's drinking water quality lags the US by 50 years and Japan by 100 years; China's 2017 average urban pipeline leakage rate was **14.71% (2018: 14.62%, with 8.179 billion tons lost)**, significantly higher than developed countries; national policies target leakage under 10% by 2020 and mandate smart water infrastructure; (2) Technology maturation — 5G, NB-IoT, cloud computing, IoT (NB-IoT enables smart meters, DMA zoning, GIS, real-time leakage monitoring); (3) Unified construction and management (统建统管) — provinces including Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hebei, Shandong, Fujian, Guangxi adopting unified secondary water supply models; (4) Rural drinking water upgrades during the 14th Five-Year Plan — estimated one county-level rural upgrade costs ~50 million RMB, implying 100-billion+ RMB market. Market size breakdown: smart water platform market projected to grow from 82.3 billion (2018) to 251.05 billion (2023E); smart water plants (prefabricated): a 3,000-ton/day plant sells for ~20 million RMB, with ~20,000 traditional water plants nationwide, market space estimated at 100+ billion RMB; pipeline network retrofit equipment estimated at 100+ billion RMB. As of H1 2020, there were ~840 smart water enterprises in China (413 manufacturing, 222 IT/software). Major tech entrants: **Huawei won Shenzhen Smart Water Phase I project for 446 million RMB (Dec 2019)**; Tencent Cloud formed strategic partnership with Guangdong Yuehai Water.

**Digital water development status (Prof. Wang Aijie, State Key Laboratory of Urban Water Resource and Environment, HIT — 2023 lecture)** [4]: A 2017-2020 survey of 194 representative water enterprises showed widespread attention and high value recognition for digital water construction. China's digital water construction is transitioning from automation and informatization toward smart/intelligent development. Water supply enterprises focus information systems on customer service (billing, WeChat public accounts, installation management); drainage enterprises focus on operational control (automation, water quality online monitoring, central control systems). Goals include unmanned water plant regulation, scientific pipeline network dispatch, and efficient process control. Half of surveyed enterprises have established independent digital management departments; leading enterprises are characterized by strong leadership attention and deep business department involvement. Government digital water procurement projects are concentrated in southeastern and central China. **China has 95 national-level research projects related to "smart + water."** China's digital water research emphasizes application and practical water issues (water quality monitoring, pollution control), **while Europe and the US focus more on theory and method innovation (big data model/algorithm development)**. Chinese digital water algorithms focus on AI-based watershed pollution tracing and risk prediction. Three urgent needs: (1) improved cognition of digitalization at the leadership level; (2) coordinated, unified construction and industry-recognized digital water standards (avoiding fragmented "each fighting for themselves"); (3) specialized digital water talent (universities lack relevant courses). Additional problems: difficulty integrating technology with business operations; **difficulty measuring digital water benefits (projects rarely generate independent economic returns)**; difficulty forming effective industrial collaboration and core technology development.

**Regulatory/policy infrastructure (CUWA official site)** [12]: The China Urban Water Association (中国城镇供水排水协会/CUWA) is a national, industry-wide, non-profit social organization founded in 1985, supervised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD). Recent key policy documents (2026): 《生态保护"十五五"规划》 (2026-08-12), 《海水淡化产业发展行动方案》 (2026-07-17), and critically **《供水条例》 (Water Supply Regulations, State Council Order No. 831), issued 2026-02-14**. CUWA history highlights: 2024 — won the 2023 National Science and Technology Progress Award First Prize; 2022 — published 《城镇水务系统碳核算与减排路径技术指南》 and 《城镇水务行业年度发展报告（2021）》; 2021 — published **《城镇水务2035年行业发展规划纲要》**; 2020 — established sponge city, water market development, smart water, and youth worker committees; 2018 — completed revision to 《城镇供水管网漏损控制及评定标准》 with Beijing Water Group.

**New Water Supply Regulations impact (Develop Technology keynote at CUWA 2026 Annual Conference, per China Daily)** [13]: At the CUWA 2026 Annual Conference (April 16-18, 2026, Shenzhen; 300+ companies), Ma Yue (马悦), General Manager of Develop Technology's Domestic Water Business Unit, explained that the new 《供水条例》 "impose rigid constraints on water source security, water quality compliance, and water pressure compliance, while linking water pricing to costs—making uncontrolled production-sales gap (产销差) directly lead to revenue loss. Pipe network leakage not only raises the production-sales gap, but also triggers water pressure fluctuations, rising water quality risks, exacerbating water source waste and operational pressure." Origin Tech (founded 2019) works with 12 UK water companies; helped prevent three billion litres of water loss; **92% of identified leaks being non-visible**. ### PART 6: COMPARISON — CHINESE vs. INTERNATIONAL WATER UTILITIES (GAPS, DIFFERENCES, SIMILARITIES)

#### 6.1 Scale and market position
- **GWI Global TOP 50 (2020)**: Veolia $19.2 billion water revenue; **BEWG 9th at $3.3 billion — the only Chinese company in top 10, up 19 positions since 2015** [62]. #### 6.2 Leakage/NRW performance
- China: urban leakage 14.71% (2017), 14.62% (2018), 12.9%/12.5% (2022), **below 9% nationally (2024)**; provincial range 10.1% (Zhejiang) to 16.7% (Liaoning) in 2022; policy target ≤9% by 2025 [5][1][14]. #### 6.3 R&D investment levels
- Chinese companies: 首创环保 R&D investment RMB 212 million in 2025 (on 18.886 billion yuan revenue — roughly 1.1% intensity) [21][22]; OriginWater R&D 343 million yuan = 4.01% of main business revenue (2024) [72]; 南方泵业 R&D 265 million yuan = 4.88% of revenue (2023) [58]; BEWG holds 772 patents + 420 software copyrights (2022) [17]; 首创环保 1,185 cumulative authorized patents (2025) [23]; OriginWater full-chain membrane IP + 60+ patents in seawater desalination [21]. 首创环保 "14th FYP" targets: R&D intensity of 2%, 120 invention patents [25].

No direct international R&D-spend-as-% of revenue figures captured, but the structural gap is in dedicated digital/AI expert headcount and global SaaS deployment scale.

#### 6.4 Technology commercialization pathways
- Chinese models: (1) franchise/PPP/BOT/ROT with minimum water volume guarantees (OriginWater) [18]; (2) light-asset transformation — BEWG's Beishui Future Technology and Beishui Cloud Services; 首创环保 light-asset orders 72.80% of new contracts [24][20]; (3) technology product launch events (BEWG BEAOA & Speed Granule "first step of technology commercialization" toward "replicable, large-scale standardized products") [17]; (4) prefabricated/assembled products (BEWG Speed Granule — China's first prefabricated municipal aerobic granular sludge product; Weipage smart water plants; Jinke New Water Island with 3-month construction, 1/6 footprint) [17][5][74]; (5) PIPP/Blue Eco-Park models selling reclaimed water to industrial B-end clients (Jinke) [74]; (6) data asset monetization — first water data asset transactions/certificates (南京, 上海城投水务, 广州水投) [32].
- International models: (1) Veolia's "technology premium" model — minority equity in investment companies, majority in operating companies, separating services into related-party contracts for fee collection at each operational stage (Qingdao case: 40% investment stake / 78% operating stake) [66]; (2) Suez's JV + concession model (Macao 25+20 year concession) [63]; (3) SaaS-based digital solution offerings (Veolia Hubgrade all solutions in SaaS mode; Suez On'connect/Aquadvanced/AssetAdvanced as products) [39][37]; (4) Metering-as-a-Service (Badger Meter netAMP subscription model) [45]; (5) Ofwat Innovation Fund competitive grants (Severn Trent £2M Water Breakthrough Challenge; £1.7 billion PR24 for smart meters) [47][46].

#### 6.5 Revenue models
- Chinese: low water prices (Beijing <1/10 of Berlin/Copenhagen; 36 key cities 1.91→2.35 yuan/ton 2013-2024); pricing formula reform (permitted costs + reasonable returns); tiered pricing 1:1.5:3; sewage treatment "government franchise, government procurement, enterprise operation" with 3-year price re-evaluations [14][29]. Reclaimed water utilization rate only 25.8% vs developed countries' 60-70% [74].
- International: French delegated management (concession and affermage/lease contracts); private companies controlled 96% of French market (Veolia 36.7%, Suez 18.8%, SAUR 40%) [69]; Veolia's average dividend yield 5.43% over 10 years [69]; UK regulatory price reviews (Ofwat PR24) with innovation funding [46]; rising block tariffs (Affinity Water WaterSave trial) [46].

#### 6.6 Patent portfolios
- Chinese: BEWG 772 patents + 420 software copyrights (2022) [17]; 首创环保 1,185 cumulative authorized patents (163 invention) [21][23]; OriginWater full-chain membrane IP, 60+ seawater desalination patents, Chinese Patent Excellence Award [21]; 津膜科技 2 National Technology Invention Second Prizes + National Science and Technology Progress First Prize (2024) [55]; 南方泵业 added 10 invention + 60 utility + 5 design patents in 2023 [58].
- International: Veolia Water Technologies 350+ patents [60]; no aggregate portfolio data captured for Suez/Anglian/PUB in gathered sources.

#### 6.7 Deployment scale of smart water systems
- China: ~840 smart water enterprises (2020) [5]; smart water market 12.48 billion yuan (2020) → 37 billion yuan (2026E) [3]; Huawei Shenzhen Smart Water Phase I 446 million RMB [5]; Shenzhen 99%+ digital coverage, 100% online monitoring via smart meters (Shenshan) [9][15]; Shantou Yuehai 632 monitoring meters, 66% remote rate, 71% of water volume monitored [11]; Chengtou Water 60+ robot applications planned by 2026 [7]; 95 national-level "smart + water" research projects [4].
- International: Veolia 10,000+ connected sites, 640+ connected sites for digital solutions, 4,400 active users, 30+ countries [36][39]; Suez 7 million smart meters deployed worldwide, 1,500+ smart water customers, 45,000 connected waste objects [37]; UK plan ~10 million smart meters by 2030 (48% coverage), 73% by 2040 [46]; Anglian 500,000+ meters fitted, 1.1M target by 2025, 1.2M more 2025-2030 [41]; Severn Trent ~600,000 meters [49]; US ~40% AMI conversion [45]; PUB Smart Water Grid with hundreds of monitoring stations [40].

#### 6.8 Regulatory incentives
- China: policy evolution from "smart water" to "smart water conservancy system" (2014-14th FYP) [3]; leakage targets (<10% by 2020, <9% by 2025) [5][14]; 15th FYP opening with Water Supply Regulations (2026) imposing rigid constraints and price-cost linkage [13]; 800亿超长期特别国债 for underground pipe networks [32]; water resource fee-to-tax nationwide Dec 2024 [32]; CUWA annual science & technology awards (e.g., Chengtou 2024 Second Prize) [8]; 3+1 rural water supply model [2]; digital China "2522" framework [4]; 100 green low-carbon benchmark sewage plants by 2025 [32]; reclaimed water 3-year action plan in 50 cities [21].
- International: Ofwat PR24 £1.7 billion for ~10 million smart meters; Water Breakthrough Challenge innovation grants [47][46]; EU Drinking Water Directive PFAS limits now binding (2026) [35]; UK Environment Agency 2050 water deficit projections (demand would exceed supply by 5 billion litres/day by 2050 without intervention) driving smart meter rollout [46].

#### 6.9 Innovation ecosystem maturity
- China: identified weaknesses — leadership cognition of digitalization; lack of unified digital water standards ("each fighting for themselves"); shortage of specialized digital water talent (universities lack courses); difficulty integrating technology with business; **difficulty measuring digital water benefits (projects rarely generate independent economic returns)**; difficulty forming effective industrial collaboration and core technology development [4]. Reliance on imported high-end equipment [1]. Technology gap versus international peers [29]. Core technology gaps in seawater desalination and industrial water (GWI's 2020 top-10 water technology breakthroughs list featured no Chinese companies) [61]. Standards differences and unfamiliarity with European/American standards hinder overseas expansion [61].
- International: mature innovation ecosystems — Veolia Hubgrade combining innovation and digital know-how across three businesses [36]; Suez Digital Solutions unit with 600+ AI experts [37]; Ofwat innovation fund ecosystem with multi-utility collaboration (Severn Trent with 4 other utilities + Microsoft, BT, Rockwell) [47]; Anglian Water Innovation Hub [43]; PUB's Smart Water Grid with Bentley machine learning [40]; satellite leak detection start-up ecosystem (Origin Tech, 12 UK water companies) [48].

#### 6.10 Similarities
- Both Chinese and international utilities are deploying digital twins, AI leak detection, smart metering (NB-IoT/WIZE/LoRa), and intelligent plant operations.
- Both are pursuing asset-light transformation and service-based revenue (Veolia operation-led model; Chinese light-asset platforms) [20][65][66].
- Both face aging infrastructure and leakage as top priorities.
- Both are integrating AI large models/agents into operations (Veolia Hubgrade AI; BEWG "Enki" vertical large model; DeepSeek deployments at Jinke/Weipage) [19][32][36].
- Both emphasize water resource recovery and membrane technology (OriginWater MBR-DF; Suez/Veolia membrane portfolios).
- Both are entering each other's domains: Chinese companies expanding overseas (United Water Dhaka; OriginWater Serbia/Russia/Malaysia; BEWG "Belt and Road"), while Veolia/Suez remain significant in China's market.

#### 6.11 Key differences / gaps summary
1. **Scale of international digital platforms**: Veolia's 10,000+ connected sites and Suez's 7 million smart meters dwarf individual Chinese utility deployments (though China's national smart water market is growing rapidly).
2. **Commercialization of digital products**: International firms monetize digital solutions as SaaS products (Hubgrade, Aquadvanced, AssetAdvanced, Metering-as-a-Service) with documented ROI (leak detection time -75%, capex -30%, energy -20%); Chinese digital water projects "rarely generate independent economic returns" [4] and are often bundled into larger construction/EPC projects.
3. **Innovation funding mechanisms**: UK Ofwat innovation funds and price reviews provide dedicated, competitive R&D funding tied to regulatory performance; China relies more on national policy mandates and SOE internal budgets.
4. **R&D focus**: China emphasizes application and practical water issues; Europe/US focus on theory, method innovation, and big data model/algorithm development [4].
5. **Market concentration & pricing**: Chinese market fragmented (top 10 = 9% concentration), water prices far below international levels, limiting funds available for innovation investment; French market historically 96% controlled by three private companies with mature delegated management.
6. **Standardization**: China lacks unified digital water standards; Europe/US have established regulatory frameworks (Ofwat, EU Drinking Water Directive) driving technology adoption.
7. **Leakage performance spread**: Best-in-class Chinese utilities (Shenzhen <5%, Shantou Yuehai 6.58%) approach international benchmarks, but national average (9% in 2024) still exceeds Japan/US (<8%) and best international performers.
8. **Patent/talent depth**: International firms maintain large dedicated digital/AI expert teams (Suez 600+; Veolia 500 experts/data scientists); Chinese firms rely more on university partnerships and national labs, with recognized talent shortages.

### PART 7: RECOMMENDED TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTIONS (技术攻关方向) — SUPPORTING EVIDENCE BASE

The research question asks for 3-5 key technology development directions for Chinese water utilities to achieve successful industrialized commercialization, tied to identified gaps and mapping to successful international commercialization models. The following evidence directly supports such recommendations:

**Direction A: AI-driven leakage control and DMA optimization** — Supported by: China's remaining leakage gap (national 9% vs. best-in-class 6.58%/below 5% [15][11], international <8% [14]); Shantou Yuehai's successful technology-enabled DMA program (365 zones, 632 meters, 71% volume monitored, 13.1%→6.58%) [11]; international models: Suez Aquadvanced (leak detection time -75%, losses -30%) [37], Thames Water/Origin Tech satellite AI (30-metre radius, 800+ leaks in trial) [48], PUB ALF machine learning digital twin [40], Veolia Waterloss Management [39], Anglian smart meters finding 100,000+ leaks [41].

**Direction B: Digital twin platforms for water networks** — Supported by: Shenzhen's digital twin adaptive dispatch (China's first "no human intervention" model; energy -5%, labor -35.6%) [9]; Chengtou Water digital twin award-winning unmanned dispatch [8]; PUB's live digital twin with ALF [40]; Veolia Hubgrade digital twin (100+ installations, 30-100% capacity/energy/chemical gains) [39][38]; Anglian/Qatium field-technician digital twins [43]; Suez Aquadvanced/AssetAdvanced [37].

**Direction C: Advanced membrane water treatment industrialization** — Supported by: China's 25.8% reclaimed water reuse vs. 60-70% international [74]; OriginWater's full-chain membrane self-reliance, MBR 70% domestic share, V-MBR energy/cost reductions, Membrane Cloud digital service system [18][72][73]; 津膜科技's CMF/SMF/MBR with National Science and Technology Progress First Prize [55]; Jinke's productization (New Water Island, 3-month construction, 1/6 footprint; PIPP model) and GWI Global Water Award [74]; membrane market 500 billion yuan projected by 2025 [21]; policy push for reclaimed water in 50 cities [21].

**Direction D: Intelligent plant unmanned operations** — Supported by: Chengtou Water "Sea-Land-Air" robot inspection (50% manual hours reduction, 60% emergency response improvement) and Nanshi smart factory (8 million yuan annual savings) [7]; BEWG "Enki" vertical large model for adaptive sewage plant control [19]; Shenzhen Bao'an adaptive dispatch [9]; international: Veolia Hubgrade Performance Plant digital twin [39]; Severn Trent AI waste catchment autonomy with £2M Ofwat funding [47]; the industry direction toward "unmanned/minimal-staffed" plants (most prefecture-level water groups expected to launch smart plant upgrades by end-2026) [53].

**Direction E: Smart metering data monetization** — Supported by: first Chinese water data asset transactions/certificates (南京, 上海城投水务, 广州水投) [32]; BEWG "Yunlian Wang" transforming water assets into data assets [19]; international: Suez 7 million smart meters with On'connect (16% customer savings) [37]; UK ~10 million smart meter plan with £1.7 billion Ofwat funding [46]; Badger Meter Metering-as-a-Service netAMP subscription model and 27 billion gallons savings [45]; Anglian £15 million annual customer savings from smart meters [41].

**Direction F: Water resource recovery** — Supported by: China's low reclaimed water utilization (25.8% vs 60-70% developed countries) [74]; OriginWater MBR-DF converting sewage to Class II/III surface water, seawater desalination breakthroughs, salt lake lithium [18][21][73]; Jinke PIPP/Blue Eco-Park industrial water sales [74]; policy timeline accelerating wastewater resource utilization (2021-2024) [21]; international: Veolia circular economy TS2A sorting with 95%+ recovery [69]; Suez industrial park circular economy services [60].

# 全球水务技术创新产业化应用研究报告（2016–2026）

## 摘要

本报告系统梳理了近十年（2016–2026）国际自来水生产及销售企业在技术创新及产业化应用方面的进展，按技术产业化应用实现的经济收益规模，排出全球前10大创新成果，涵盖智能水表/AMI、海水淡化能量回收、膜法水处理、数字孪生、AI漏损检测、MBR、PFAS处理、智能泵、磷回收及大规模水回用等领域。报告同时对比分析了中国同类水务企业在技术创新与产业化能力方面的差距与相似之处，并基于中外标杆实践，提出国内水务企业应重点攻关的五大技术方向，旨在推动技术创新成果实现规模化、产业化应用。

---

## 一、研究背景与排序说明

### 1.1 研究范围与标准

本报告聚焦**自来水生产及销售企业（水务运营企业）**及其产业链上的核心技术供应商，时间跨度为2016–2026年。纳入排名的创新成果须满足以下条件：

- **已完成产业化应用**（非仅停留在研发或中试阶段）；
- **已产生可量化的经济收益**（包括企业营收、利润、成本节约、水资源回收价值等）；
- 具有**规模化部署**证据（如覆盖用户数、处理规模、合同金额等）。

### 1.2 全球水务行业格局概览

根据全球水智库（Global Water Intelligence, GWI）2025年发布的全球水务企业排名，**威立雅（Veolia）**以约125亿欧元的水务收入位居全球第一，为近9500万人提供供水服务；**艺康（Ecolab）**位列第二；**赛莱默（Xylem）**以约86亿美元的水技术收入位列第三，2023年完成对懿华（Evoqua）75亿美元的收购后，成为全球最大的纯水技术企业[1]。**北控水务**是全球前10名中唯一的中国企业，2020年以约33亿美元的水务收入排名第9位[2]。

在行业整体格局中，**智慧水务技术、PFAS处理、脱碳项目、循环经济倡议**被GWI列为推动行业发展的四大核心力量[1]。

---

## 二、国际水务技术创新产业化应用前10名（按经济收益规模排序）

### 第1名：智能水表与高级计量基础设施（AMI）

**代表企业：Badger Meter（美国）、Xylem/赛莱默（美国）、SUEZ/苏伊士（法国）**

**技术创新成果**：以蜂窝网络（NB-IoT/Cellular）通信为核心的智能水表及高级计量基础设施（AMI），配套软件即服务（SaaS）数据平台，实现用水数据的实时采集、远程抄表、漏损监测与用户用水行为分析。

**产业化应用情况**：

- **Badger Meter**是全球智能水表AMI领域的标杆企业。2025财年实现净销售额**9.167亿美元**，净利润1.416亿美元，摊薄每股收益4.79美元，经营性现金流1.837亿美元[3]。2024年全年净销售额8.266亿美元，同比增长18%，营业利润率创下19.1%的历史纪录[4]。2025年1月，公司以1.84亿美元收购了SmartCover Systems（下水道/泵站监测领域美国市占率约50%的细分龙头）[3]。其最具标志性的产业化项目是获得**波多黎各水务局（PRASA）**合同——全球最大规模的AMI部署之一，覆盖**160万个服务连接**，采用E系列超声波水表、ORION蜂窝终端和BEACON SaaS平台[3]。截至2026年，美国约**40%的已安装水表已升级为AMI**，Badger Meter的AMI解决方案已实现约270亿加仑的潜在节水量[5]。
- **Xylem**于2016年以约**17亿美元现金**收购Sensus，后者在全球安装了超过8000万台计量设备，2016财年调整后收入8.37亿美元、调整后EBITDA 1.59亿美元，收购价对应10.7倍EBITDA[6]。2025年，Xylem宣布将北美以外的国际水/热计量业务出售给AURELIUS，该业务2024年收入约2.5亿美元，Xylem保留北美Sensus品牌智能计量业务[7]。
- **SUEZ**在全球部署了**700万个智能水表**，其ON'connect系列产品通过减少消耗和检测泄漏可节水高达16%，每户每年节省最高200欧元[8]。法国勒芒大都会项目自2018年起部署12万个智能水表，夜间流量减少30立方米/小时（相当于每年节水25万立方米、节约12.5万欧元）[9]。

**经济收益证据**：全球智能水表市场2025年规模约**68亿美元**（Bluefield Research），智能计量系统占水务企业数字支出的20%以上[10]；AMI水表全球市场2024年为16亿美元，预计2034年达223亿美元，CAGR约30%[11]。Badger Meter近十年收入CAGR约9%，盈利CAGR约17%[12]。

---

### 第2名：海水淡化与能量回收技术

**代表企业：Energy Recovery Inc.（美国）、ACWA Power（沙特）**

**技术创新成果**：等压式能量回收装置（PX® Pressure Exchanger®）——通过旋转导管将浓盐水的高压能量直接传递给进水，峰值能量回收效率达**98%**，可使海水反渗透（SWRO）淡化能耗降低**60%**，已成为全球SWRO行业的标配技术[13]。

**产业化应用情况**：

- **Energy Recovery Inc.（ERII）**是全球海水淡化能量回收领域的绝对龙头。截至2023年，已向全球100多个国家供应超过**3.5万台PX设备**，技术每年为客户节约超过**140亿千瓦时**电能，日产清洁水超过120亿升[14]。公司2023年营收1.283亿美元，总资产2.53亿美元[14]。2026年，公司在沙特达曼附近签约建设新制造基地，为麦加、巴哈、阿西尔地区百万人供水安全提供保障[15]。
- 标志性项目包括：**Taweelah IWP**（阿联酋，全球最大RO海水淡化厂，日产能90.9万立方米，2022年投产）；**Rabigh 3 IWP**（沙特，日产能60万立方米，为麦加地区供水，电耗降至**3.2千瓦时/立方米以下**，年节电约5亿千瓦时、减碳约23.5万吨）[16]；**Hassyan IWP**（迪拜，日产能81.8万立方米，创下**0.365美元/立方米**的全球最低水价纪录）[17]。
- **ACWA Power**目前拥有**950万立方米/日**的淡化水产能组合，在沙特、阿联酋、摩洛哥等14个国家运营16座海水淡化厂，满足沙特30%的用水需求[18][19]。

**经济收益证据**：全球能量回收装置（ERD）市场2024年达**21亿美元**，预计2033年达52亿美元，CAGR 10.2%[20]。ERII技术为客户带来的年度能源成本节约总额高达**72亿美元**[15]。

---

### 第3名：膜法水处理与反渗透（RO）技术

**代表企业：DuPont Water Solutions（美国杜邦水处理）**

**技术创新成果**：以FilmTec™反渗透膜、纳滤膜和离子交换树脂为核心的全系列水处理膜产品体系，以及基于AI的设计工具WAVE PRO。杜邦水处理每分钟处理约5000万加仑水，其中离子交换+RO占产品组合约80%，超过70%的销售为替换销售[21]。

**产业化应用情况**：

- 杜邦水处理2021年净销售额约**14亿美元**，员工约2200人，过半收入来自亚太地区，2019–2022年有机销售增速约7%，为GDP增速的两倍以上，毛利率"远高于30%"[21]。
- 2024年5月，杜邦宣布将分拆为三家独立上市公司，水处理业务将独立上市[22]。2025年12月推出FilmTec™ SW30XLE-400/34新型RO膜元件，初始压降降低25%[23]。
- WAVE PRO设计工具已扩展至RO和纳滤领域，拥有4000多名专业用户，被100多篇技术期刊引用，近三年下载量超1.6万次[24]。
- 产业化应用覆盖全球数千个市政和工业水处理项目，包括海水淡化、苦咸水淡化、超纯水制备、污水回用等场景。

**经济收益证据**：全球反渗透（RO）市场2025年约**87亿美元**，预计2034年达182亿美元，CAGR 8.6%；薄膜复合（TFC）膜占72.4%份额，前十大企业占据约55–60%的收入份额[25]。全球膜法水处理市场2025年约64.7亿美元[26]。

---

### 第4名：数字孪生与管网智能分析平台

**代表企业：Veolia/威立雅（法国）、SUEZ/苏伊士（法国）、Autodesk/欧特克（美国）、PUB新加坡公用事业局**

**技术创新成果**：基于物联网、大数据和AI的水务数字孪生平台，包括威立雅Hubgrade系列、苏伊士AQUADVANCED®系列、欧特克Innovyze系列以及新加坡PUB的实时数字孪生管网系统。

**产业化应用情况**：

- **Veolia Hubgrade**：在全球20多个国家设有约60个监控中心，由450多名专家和数据科学家运营，监控超过**300万个传感器**（含100万个智能水表）和30万个数据点。2023年起在全球范围内推广AI驱动解决方案，覆盖**1万多个互联站点**。自2017年以来，Hubgrade在布拉格实现了市政管网漏损率降低15%[27][28]。其"Hubgrade Wastewater Plant Performance"数字孪生模块已在全球**100多个污水处理厂**部署，可实现曝气能耗降低30%、化学品消耗降低100%、生物处理能力提升40%、水处理能力提升100%[29]。
- **SUEZ AQUADVANCED®**：全球领先的供水管网实时管理软件，可将漏损检测时间缩短**75%**、水损降低至少**30%**、能耗降低最高20%，投资回报期不到1年。已在巴塞罗那（覆盖4600公里管网、390万人口）、米兰（单位水能耗降低8%、年减碳2600吨）、丹佛水务（150万用户管网更换规划）等全球50多个城市部署[8][30]。
- **Autodesk/Innovyze**：2021年3月以**10亿美元**收购Innovyze——全球最大的纯水务基础设施软件提供商，拥有约3000家企业客户[31]。Innovyze产品（InfoWorks ICM、InfoWorks WS Pro、Info360 Insight）在全球水务建模和数字孪生领域占据领先地位。
- **新加坡PUB**：部署数百个管网监测站，构建了新加坡供水管网的高保真**实时数字孪生**系统，利用机器学习算法持续校准和训练模型，其"Anomaly Leak Finder（ALF）"算法可自动检测隐蔽漏点并定位。2022年新加坡每100公里管道报告漏损4.1起，数字孪生使隐蔽漏损检测效率大幅提升[32]。

## 三、中国同类水务企业对比分析

### 3.1 中国水务行业整体发展现状

中国水务行业已进入"高质量发展阶段"。2024年全国总用水量稳定在5928亿立方米，万元GDP用水量和万元工业增加值用水量较2020年分别下降17.7%和23.6%，城市公共供水管网漏损率降至**9%以下**，农村自来水普及率达94%[64]。

智慧水务市场方面，2020年中国智慧水务服务市场规模约**124.8亿元**，预计2026年达**370亿元**[65]。智慧水务平台+智慧水厂+管网改造设备三大板块合计市场空间超过**3000亿元**，但行业集中度极低，头部上市公司市占率不足1%[66]。截至2020年上半年，全国约有840家智慧水务企业[66]。

政策层面，2026年2月国务院发布《供水条例》（国务院令第831号），对水源安全、水质达标、水压达标提出刚性约束，并将水价与成本挂钩，使产销差失控直接转化为收入损失，倒逼水务企业加速数字化转型[67]。

### 3.2 中国代表性水务企业创新与产业化情况

#### （1）北控水务集团（0371.HK）

北控水务是中国规模最大的水务企业，总资产、总收入和水处理规模均居国内行业第一，连续16年蝉联"中国水业十大影响力企业"榜首。2020年拥有1334座水厂（1115座污水、174座供水、43座再生水、2座海水淡化），总设计处理能力4212万吨/日[2]。

技术创新方面，北控水务2022年发布两大技术产品：**BEAOA技术**（与中国工程院院士彭永臻合作）——新型高效深度脱氮除磷工艺，总氮去除率超85%、节省曝气能耗25%以上、除磷药剂减少40%–100%、实现零碳源投加和30%原位污泥减量，已在北京、山东、海南、广西等地项目应用；**北控速粒**——国内首个基于好氧颗粒污泥的预制化/装配式市政污水处理产品，节能20%以上、占地减少50%、工期缩短2/3、投资节省20%以上，适用于2万吨/日以下的中小规模场景[68]。截至2022年4月，北控水务拥有**772项专利、420项软件著作权**和10项省部级科技奖项[68]。

2025年，北控水务推出水务行业垂直大模型**"Enki"**（运营智慧大脑），以及"云链网"工业互联网平台，提出"将水务资产转化为数据资产"[69]。

#### （2）首创环保集团（600008.SH）

首创环保2025年营收188.86亿元，归母净利润17.72亿元，水处理能力2728万吨/日，业务覆盖29个省份190多个城市。**2025年研发投入2.12亿元**，累计授权专利**1185项**（含发明专利163项），研发人员296人[70][71]。

其核心创新成果**CAPITAL CREATE®好氧颗粒污泥技术**（"蓝水工厂"）在浙江海宁实现商业化应用——处理能力从4万吨/日提升至7万吨/日（**在不增加土地的情况下产能提升75%**），能耗降低54%、实现零碳源投加[71]。**ASMART®智能控制系统**将项目实施周期缩短50%；**WEAM智慧运营平台**已在30多个项目中应用；"数字厂长1.0"AI智慧运营系统与清华大学联合开发[71][72]。2025年智能加药系统在呼和浩特降低药耗12.20%，北京东坝碳源投加降低14.50%，全年药剂成本节约1200万元[70]。产销差率连续9年下降，2025年实际值12.20%[70]。

#### （3）碧水源（300070.SZ）

碧水源是中国膜法水处理的龙头企业，**MBR膜占据中国膜法水处理市场70%以上份额**，日水处理量超过2200万吨，年高品质再生水产水量超70亿吨。2024年研发投入**3.43亿元**，占主营业务收入**4.01%**，研发人员519人[73][74]。

核心技术覆盖微滤、超滤、纳滤、反渗透全膜链自主知识产权。**MBR-DF双膜新水源工艺**可将市政污水转化为地表水II/III类高品质水源；**V-MBR振动膜生物反应器**较传统MBR能耗降低20%以上、运行成本降低10%以上[75]。标志性项目包括：北京密云再生水项目（4.5万吨/日，国内首个大规模MBR，打破GE、西门子、陶氏垄断）、武汉北湖污水处理厂（80万吨/日，全球最大单期MBR）、北京高碑店再生水厂（100万吨/日）、青岛董家口海水淡化（10万吨/日，首个自主技术大规模海水淡化）、山东鲁北海水淡化（15万吨/日）[75][76]。

2025年，碧水源发布**"膜力云"智慧水务全流程服务体系**，实现膜技术与数字化、智能化的融合；工业膜订单增长30%，成功替代杜邦RO膜（华泰纸业）和GE超滤膜（陶之湾水厂），加速膜产品国产替代[76]。

#### （4）深圳环境水务集团

深圳环境水务集团是中国智慧水务的标杆。2026年中国水协年会上披露：**数字化覆盖率99%以上，数字孪生系统使运维效率提升30%，客户满意度97%，管网漏损率低于5%**（世界领先水平）[77]。

其入选2024年智慧水务典型案例的三个项目包括：**基于在线水力模型和人工智能的供水自适应调度**——首创国内"无人干预、实时调度、秒级计算、智能优化、精准调压"的供水自适应调度模式，实现配水能耗降低约5%、综合电耗降低约3.5%、人工成本降低35.6%[78]；**深水云脑**驱动的"数字排水-水环境管理平台"；以及**深汕水务全要素智慧运营管理平台**——覆盖"源、厂、站、网、河、湖、海"全水循环，智能水表在线监测覆盖率100%[78]。

#### （5）上海城投水务

上海城投水务是中国首家取得数据资产登记证书的国有企业。其**南市水厂"1+2+1+N"智慧工厂体系**（一个数字孪生平台、水量水质双模型、一套MES管理系统、N个机器人）历时五年建成，被认定为2025年上海市先进级智慧工厂，实现出水水质100%达标、**年成本节约超过800万元**。其**"海陆空"机器人巡检系统**（泰和污水处理厂）是中国首个污水处理厂三维机器人智能巡检系统，覆盖五大核心场景，自动识别21项安全风险和5项工艺状态，人工巡检时间减少50%、应急响应时间提升60%[79]。

城投水务制水公司"数字水厂智能无人调度实现路径技术研究及示范应用"项目获**2024年度中国城镇供水排水协会科学技术奖二等奖**，基于流体力学、AI和大数据构建智能无人调度系统，实现进出水量和加药量的自动调节[80]。

#### （6）粤海水务

粤海水务管理运营着香港东深供水工程（对港供水占香港淡水需求70–80%），2017年总水处理规模2507万吨/日，位居全国第二[81]。截至2022年，在全国运营110多个水务项目，日处理能力超5600万吨，服务人口超9400万[82]。

其智慧管网漏损检测项目（获广东省科技进步奖）**年节水超4700万吨、降低生产成本超2300万元**。东莞常平水司借助其技术将漏损率从20.77%降至10%以下，电耗降低21.07%，年效益超700万元。2020年与华为合作建立**中国首个鲲鹏智慧水务联合创新实验室**，基于鲲鹏计算产业生态打造城市全域水系统智慧化平台[82][83]。

### 3.3 中外差距与差异对比分析

#### （1）漏损率差距

中国城市公共供水管网漏损率从2017年的14.71%降至2024年的**9%以下**，但各省份差异显著（2022年辽宁16.7%、广东12.0%、浙江10.1%），仍高于日本和美国（均低于8%）[84][66]。深圳（<5%）和汕头粤海（6.58%）等标杆企业已达到国际先进水平[77][85]。国际方面，Veolia在布拉格实现漏损率降低15%[27]，SUEZ宣称可降低水损至少30%[8]，英国Anglian Water每公里管网的漏损量仅为其他英国水务公司的一半[86]。

#### （2）研发投入与技术积累差距

中国头部水务企业研发投入强度在1%–4%之间（首创环保约1.1%、碧水源4.01%、南方泵业4.88%）[70][73][87]。国际方面，威立雅水务技术拥有**350多项专利**，苏伊士数字解决方案部门拥有**600多名数据和AI专家**[88][89]。中国企业在专利数量上增长迅速（北控水务772项、首创环保1185项），但在**基础算法、核心模型、高端传感器等底层技术**方面仍存在差距。哈尔滨工业大学王爱杰教授2023年的调研指出：中国数字水务研究强调应用和解决实际水问题，**而欧洲和美国更注重理论和方法创新（大数据模型/算法开发）**；中国数字水务面临"数字化效益难以量化（项目很少产生独立的经济回报）""缺乏统一的数字水务标准""数字化人才短缺"三大痛点[90]。

#### （3）商业化路径差距

国际水务企业的技术创新商业化已形成成熟的**产品化、SaaS化**模式：威立雅Hubgrade全部解决方案以SaaS模式提供[29]；苏伊士AQUADVANCED®/AssetAdvanced®以标准化产品在全球复制（AssetAdvanced已在50多个客户、服务约7500万人口）[8]；Badger Meter推出"Metering-as-a-Service"订阅模式[5]；英国Ofwat通过监管价格审查（PR24）为智能水表部署提供**17亿英镑**专项资金，并通过创新基金竞争性资助（如Severn Trent获得200万英镑AI污水管网自治项目）[91][92]。

相比之下，中国水务企业的数字化项目多为**定制化EPC工程**，与土建和设备捆绑，难以独立产生可量化的经济回报[90]。中国水务企业正在探索轻资产转型（北控水务设立北水未来科技和北水云服两家轻资产平台公司；首创环保2025年新签合同中轻资产服务和技术产品订单占72.80%[72]），但整体仍以重资产投资运营为主。

#### （4）市场规模与集中度差距

中国供水市场前十大企业集中度仅**9%**，供水市场80%为国有、10%私营、10%外资；污水领域48%国有、30%外资、22%私营[93]。法国供水市场历史上由三家私营公司控制96%的市场（威立雅36.7%、苏伊士18.8%、SAUR 40%）[94]。中国智慧水务行业约840家企业，头部上市公司市占率不足1%[66]，碎片化格局制约了技术标准的统一和规模化推广。

#### （5）水价机制差距

中国36个重点城市居民水价2013–2024年仅从1.91元/吨涨至2.35元/吨（CAGR约1.9%），**北京水价不到柏林或哥本哈根的1/10**，悉尼、新加坡、伦敦、巴黎的水价是北京的6–7倍[95]。低水价压缩了水务企业的利润空间，限制了技术创新投入能力。2021年修订的《城镇供水价格管理办法》引入"准许成本+合理收益"的定价公式，2024年新一轮水价调整已在多省市启动，水资源费改税于2024年12月在全国推行，水价机制改革正在加速[96]。

#### （6）共同点与相似之处

中外水务企业均将**数字化转型**作为核心战略：中国企业在AI大模型应用上甚至走在前列（北控水务"Enki"垂直大模型、金科环境"水萝卜"AI助手、威派格河图AI接入DeepSeek）[69][96]。双方都在部署数字孪生、AI漏损检测、智能水表（NB-IoT/WIZE/LoRa）和智能水厂。双方都在探索轻资产转型和服务化收入模式。双方都高度重视膜法水处理和水资源循环利用（碧水源MBR-DF双膜工艺与苏伊士/威立雅的膜产品组合形成直接竞争）。

## 四、国内水务企业重点技术攻关方向建议

基于上述对比分析，针对中国水务企业技术创新产业化能力提升，提出以下五大重点技术攻关方向：

### 方向一：AI驱动的漏损控制与DMA分区计量技术

**攻关理由**：中国管网漏损率（全国平均9%，2024年）虽已显著下降，但仍高于日本和美国（<8%），且各省份差距悬殊（辽宁16.7% vs 浙江10.1%）[84]。漏损控制是水务企业最直接的经济效益来源——国际实践已充分验证：SUEZ可将漏损检测时间缩短75%、水损降低30%以上[8]；FIDO AI在英国实现25%–37%的漏损降低[97]；泰晤士水务用AI卫星技术（Origin Orbit®）在18周试验中定位800多处漏点，日均节水870万升[98]；汕头粤海水务通过三年行动计划（365个三级分区、632个监测表计、71%水量在线监测），将综合漏损率从13.1%降至6.58%[85]。

**攻关要点**：开发适配中国管网特征（复杂环状管网、多水源切换、大口径输水干管）的AI漏损定位算法；研发低成本、长寿命、自供电的管网智能感知终端；构建"分区计量（DMA）+夜间最小流量分析+声学/压力波融合定位"的标准化漏损控制产品体系，形成可复制的SaaS化服务平台。

**产业化路径**：参考FIDO Tech的DaaS模式和SUEZ的标准化产品模式，将漏损控制从"项目定制"转变为"产品化输出"，实现跨区域复制。

### 方向二：水务管网数字孪生平台

**攻关理由**：全球水务数字孪生市场2025年约28亿美元、预计2034年达84亿美元[33]。新加坡PUB的数字孪生管网已实现隐蔽漏点自动检测[32]；Veolia Hubgrade数字孪生模块在100多个水厂部署，可实现曝气能耗降30%、化学品消耗降100%[29]；丹麦Køge污水厂借助数字孪生将水处理能力提升35%–60%、电耗降低35%[99]。中国深圳已建成全国首个"无人干预、实时调度"的自适应供水调度系统（配水能耗降5%、人工成本降35.6%）[78]，上海城投水务的数字孪生水厂年节约成本超800万元[79]，但全国范围内仍以定制化项目为主，缺乏可规模化复制的产品。

**攻关要点**：突破水务机理模型与AI数据驱动的融合建模技术；开发国产化水力模型引擎（替代EPANET等国外工具）；构建供水管网"数字孪生+仿真推演+智能调度"一体化平台；建立数字孪生效益评估标准体系。

**产业化路径**：参考Autodesk/Innovyze以10亿美元并购实现软件产品化的路径[31]，推动国内水务软件企业的整合与产品化，形成"平台+生态"的商业闭环。

### 方向三：先进膜法水处理技术的产业化

**攻关理由**：中国城市再生水利用率2021年仅**25.8%**，远低于发达国家的60%–70%[100]。中国膜产业市场2022年达3600亿元、2023年达4300亿元，预计2025年达5000亿元[100]。碧水源已实现全膜链自主知识产权（MBR占国内70%市场份额），金科环境的纳滤水厂项目获2022年GWI全球水奖"最佳市政水项目"[101]，但在高端RO膜、纳滤膜、特种分离膜领域仍部分依赖进口。国际对标：杜邦水处理年销售额14亿美元、70%以上为替换销售[21]；全球RO市场2025年87亿美元[25]。

**攻关要点**：攻关海水淡化反渗透膜、工业零排放特种膜、盐湖提锂膜等高端膜材料的国产化；开发"膜法+数字化"结合的膜污染智能预测与运维系统（对标Veolia Smart Membranes云端膜诊断工具[29]）；推广MBR-DF双膜新水源工艺，将污水直接转化为工业用水和生态补水。

**产业化路径**：参考碧水源"膜更换"国产替代策略和金科环境PIPP（公共-产业-私营合作）模式——将高品质再生水直接销售给工业企业，形成可复制的商业模式[101][76]。

### 方向四：智能水厂无人化运行技术

**攻关理由**：人工成本是水务企业运营成本的重要组成部分，无人化/少人化是行业明确趋势。上海城投水务的"海陆空"机器人巡检系统使人工巡检时间减少50%、应急响应时间提升60%[79]；南市水厂智慧工厂年节约成本超800万元[79]；北控水务"Enki"大模型实现污水厂自适应控制[69]。到2026年底，预计大多数地级市水务集团将启动智慧水厂升级或管网漏损控制项目[102]。

**攻关要点**：开发水厂全流程智能控制算法（进水-工艺-出水-加药全链条自动调节）；研制水厂巡检机器人、管道检测机器人、水质自动检测机器人等装备体系；构建"数字孪生+AI大模型+机器人"三位一体的无人化水厂整体解决方案。

**产业化路径**：参考Veolia Hubgrade Performance Plant以SaaS模式在100多个水厂复制的经验[29]，将无人化水厂技术标准化、模块化，向中小水厂输出。

### 方向五：智能计量与数据资产化

**攻关理由**：智能水表是水务数字化的入口，也是数据资产化的基础。全球智能水表市场2025年约68亿美元[10]，美国约40%的水表已升级为AMI[5]，英国计划到2030年安装近1000万个智能水表（Ofwat PR24提供17亿英镑资金）[91]。中国方面，南京完成首笔水务数据资产交易、上海城投水务获得首张国企数据资产登记证书，水务数据资产化已进入实操阶段[96]。北控水务"云链网"平台提出"将水务资产转化为数据资产"[69]。

**攻关要点**：攻关高精度、长寿命、低功耗的超声波及电磁智能水表核心传感器技术；建设水务数据资产确权、评估、交易的标准体系；开发基于智能计量数据的用户增值服务（漏水提醒、用水行为分析、阶梯水价优化）；探索"Metering-as-a-Service"订阅制商业模式（对标Badger Meter netAMP模式[5]）。

**产业化路径**：借鉴Anglian Water智能水表项目（安装50多万只、帮助用户发现10万多个漏点、年节省客户水费约1500万英镑）的经济效益验证方法[86]，建立中国智能水表部署的量化效益评估体系，为大规模推广提供依据。

---

## 五、结论

过去十年，全球水务技术创新产业化呈现出清晰的趋势：**数字化技术（智能计量、AI漏损检测、数字孪生）正在取代传统工程设备，成为水务企业经济收益增长的主要引擎**；膜法水处理、海水淡化能量回收等绿色技术持续创造大规模经济价值；PFAS处理等新兴监管驱动型市场快速崛起。

中国水务企业在市场规模、工程能力和膜技术国产化方面取得了显著进步，北控水务、首创环保、碧水源、深圳环境水务集团等企业在智慧水务和膜技术领域已达到国际先进水平。但与威立雅、苏伊士、赛莱默等国际巨头相比，在**数字化产品的SaaS化商业化能力、基础算法与底层技术积累、行业标准化程度、水价机制与创新激励机制**等方面仍存在明显差距。

未来五年（2026–2030），中国水务企业应以"AI驱动漏损控制与DMA分区计量、数字孪生平台、先进膜法水处理产业化、智能水厂无人化运行、智能计量与数据资产化"五大方向为重点攻关领域，从"项目定制"转向"产品化输出"，从"重资产运营"转向"轻资产技术服务"，最终实现技术创新成果的规模化、产业化商业应用。
